_schema.block: Root BEM class (what the root element gets). null only for Form (no HeroUI CSS). For CalendarYearPicker and Dropdown no element carries it (see blockNote).
_schema.blockNote: Present only where the `block` class is not applied to any element.
_schema.extraBlocks: Additional BEM blocks the same React component also emits (e.g. Table -> table-root + table, Toast -> toast + toast-region). `elements` can belong to an extra block: Table block is table-root but its elements are table__* (derive the element name by splitting on "__", not by slicing the block length).
_schema.props: DESIGN axis: prop -> allowed values. Sources: tailwind-variants `variants` (authoritative), attribute-driven design props (orientation, placement, hideSeparator, visibility ...; see attrProps) and design props cascaded from a wrapper to children by context (see cascadedProps). Generic runtime STATE props (isSelected, isDisabled, isInvalid, isIndeterminate, disabled, isPending, isEmpty, isYearPickerOpen) are NOT in props: they live in attrProps + stateAttrs. Boolean props are [true,false].
_schema.cascadedProps: prop -> {to: [child component names], via: React context}. These props are accepted by the wrapper, put NO class on it (unless modifierFor says so) and are forwarded to children; the child classes are listed in modifierTargets. A static author must write those child classes on every child.
_schema.attrProps: props with NO modifier class that change styling through a data attribute React sets (CSS keys on [data-...=value]); includes generic state props (those are not copied into `props`). Fields: values, default, attr (the attribute), target (elements carrying it), optional note/valueMap.
_schema.propTargets: prop -> the part/element that actually receives the prop when it is NOT the root (e.g. Modal size lives on Modal.Container), or "Root (cascades to X via context)".
_schema.defaults: tv defaultVariants merged with literal defaults in the React Root signature (e.g. Tabs orientation = "horizontal"). A prop without a default adds no class.
_schema.rootDefaults: Other literal default values in the React Root signature that are not style props.
_schema.modifierFor: prop -> value -> class(es) added to the ROOT element (the element carrying `block`): a string (space separated when several) or null. ALWAYS string|null, never an object. null = no class lands on the root: the value is the default, or the tv class has no CSS rule (see inertClasses), or the class lands on a different element (see modifierTargets), or the prop is attribute-driven (see attrProps). Boolean props use the keys "true"/"false".
_schema.modifierTargets: prop -> value -> {"<element class>": "<modifier class(es)>"}: the COMPLETE element-level mapping, present only for values where some CSS-backed class lands on an element other than the root (Modal size lg -> {"modal__dialog":"modal__dialog--lg"}) or on a cascaded child (TextField variant secondary -> {"input":"input--secondary", ...}). The key is the element class that must receive the modifier. Where the root also gets a class it is repeated here under the block key.
_schema.inertClasses: "prop.value" -> class(es) that React/tv emits but for which NO rule exists in heroui.min.css (adding them is a no-op), e.g. button--md.
_schema.inertSlotClasses: Slot classes React emits (tv slots) for which NO rule exists in heroui.min.css, e.g. slider__marks, switch__icon, disclosure__heading.
_schema.slotClasses: Raw tailwind-variants slot map: slot key -> BEM class (what each slot emits). Components whose tv has no slots omit it.
_schema.parts: React compound sub-component (e.g. Card.Header) -> BEM element class it renders, or null when it renders no BEM-class element (RAC wrapper, SVG arrow styled via [data-slot], non-DOM API). Classes may be a block of another component when a part delegates (Menu.Item -> menu-item).
_schema.partDetails: Per part: tag = element React renders (dom.<tag>) when the part renders a plain element; dataSlot = the data-slot React sets (CSS sometimes keys on it); otherSlots = further slots the same part function also renders (inner wrappers); reuses = other HeroUI component the part delegates to; why = reason for manual mapping; fixedBy = correction source.
_schema.elements: Every .block__element class found in heroui.min.css for the owned blocks (modifier suffix stripped).
_schema.cssOnlyClasses: Classes that exist in the CSS but are not produced by any tv definition; reactLiteral=true means React hardcodes them outside tv (author must add by hand when the condition applies); false means React never emits them (dead/optional CSS).
_schema.stateAttrs: data-* / aria-* attribute names the CSS selects on for this block or its elements (global theme/motion flags excluded; see globalAttrs). stateAttrValues gives the literal values the selectors test; the HTML author sets those on the matching element.
_schema.otherAttrSelectors: Non data/aria attribute selectors in the CSS for this block (role=..., slot=..., type=...).
_schema.cssDataSlots: [data-slot=...] values the CSS of this block selects on. React sets these on children; static HTML must set the same data-slot value on those children.
_schema.runtimeCssVars: Custom properties the CSS of this block reads but that are declared nowhere in the stylesheet (React/RAC set them inline at runtime). See top-level runtimeCssVars for who sets each.
_schema.notes: What an HTML author must add by hand that React/React Aria normally adds at runtime.

contractWarnings: data-slot collision: HeroUI CSS itself selects on [data-slot=label] (35 rules), [data-slot=description] (20), [data-slot=field-error], [data-slot=input], [data-slot=list-box], [data-slot=separator] and 54 other values: 60 distinct data-slot values in 344 selector occurrences (see each component cssDataSlots). A design kit that uses data-slot="label" for ITS OWN child-part markup will trigger those selectors. Decide whether kit attributes are rewritten (e.g. data-hero-part) before emitting HeroUI HTML, or whether they are passed through on purpose.

Some RAC state attributes (data-hovered, data-pressed, data-disabled on native controls) have pseudo-class twins (:hover, :active, :disabled) in the CSS, so they are only needed to force a state in a static mock; data-focus-visible does NOT (see next item). Attributes without a pseudo-class twin (data-selected, data-open, data-expanded, data-invalid, data-placeholder, data-orientation, data-placement, data-empty, data-pending, ...) must be written by hand to render that state.

Keyboard focus rings: 36 rules use the selector `:focus-visible:not(:focus)`, which can never match natively (an element matching :focus-visible always matches :focus); the ring is only drawn through the other selector of the same rule, [data-focus-visible=true], which React Aria sets. Static HTML that wants a visible focus ring must write data-focus-visible="true" (on the element RAC sets it on: e.g. the content label for Checkbox/Radio/Switch).

Overlay components (Modal, AlertDialog, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, Select/ComboBox/Autocomplete/Dropdown popovers, Toast region) are positioned at runtime by React Aria with inline styles; the CSS only partly provides layout. See each component notes and runtimeCssVars.

data-theme.note: On <html> or any ancestor (or use classes .light/.dark/.default). Token sets; required for colours to resolve outside :root defaults.

data-vibrant-palette.note: Ancestor flag that swaps to the vibrant palette (CSS has separate light and dark variants).

data-reduce-motion.note: Ancestor flag read by ~1000 selectors via :is([data-reduce-motion=true], [data-reduce-motion=true] *). Transitions/animations are applied only when it is NOT true; a static mock needs nothing.

data-scrollbar.note: Ancestor flag consumed by the .scrollbar utility.

dir.note: Ancestor dir=rtl flips directional rules (8 selectors).

--color-field-border-invalid.setBy: Declared nowhere in the stylesheet and set by no HeroUI/RAC source, yet read WITHOUT a fallback in the [data-invalid=true] rules of input-group, color-input-group, number-field, search-field and date-input-group, so the invalid border-colour falls back to the property initial value (currentcolor; browser result unverified). Define it yourself on :root (e.g. --color-field-border-invalid: var(--danger)) to get a red border.

--table-row-level.setBy: react-aria-components Table (tree rows) inline style on rows.

--trigger-width.setBy: react-aria-components Popover inline style (px width of the trigger element); HeroUI Autocomplete also passes it. Static HTML: set to the trigger width, e.g. style="--trigger-width:240px".

Accordion.notes: DOM: div.accordion[data-slot=accordion] > div.accordion__item (direct siblings; separator is ::after, absent on :last-child) > h3.accordion__heading (RAC Heading level 3) > button.accordion__trigger[type=button][slot=trigger][data-slot=accordion-trigger][id=T][aria-controls=P][aria-expanded=true|false]; then div.accordion__panel[id=P][role=group][aria-labelledby=T] > div.accordion__body > div.accordion__body-inner. React auto-adds the inner div (no part fn): Body className lands on the INNER div, other props on the outer. data-slot=accordion-trigger on the trigger is REQUIRED by CSS (accordion--surface rounds first/last item via [data-slot=accordion-trigger]). Indicator part (author places it, conventionally INSIDE the trigger after the label): with no children it renders the default svg.accordion__indicator[data-slot=accordion-indicator] 16x16 chevron-down (viewBox 0 0 16 16, fill none, aria-hidden=true, role=presentation, path fill=currentColor fill-rule=evenodd clip-rule=evenodd d="M2.97 5.47a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0L8 9.44l3.97-3.97a.75.75 0 1 1 1.06 1.06l-4.5 4.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06 0l-4.5-4.5a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.06"); ml-auto size-4; a custom child element gets the class + data-slot + data-expanded via cloneElement. EXPANDED item: aria-expanded="true" on trigger (hover bg is suppressed by :not([aria-expanded=true])); data-expanded="true" on .accordion__indicator (rotates -180deg) and on .accordion__panel (REQUIRED: panel is opacity:0 without it); RAC also puts data-expanded="true" on .accordion__item (no CSS). Panel height = var(--disclosure-panel-height), set inline by RAC on the panel: "auto" when open, "0px" when closed, px only mid-animation; if unset, height is auto, so open panels need no inline style. COLLAPSED: hidden="until-found" + aria-hidden="true" + style="--disclosure-panel-height:0px" on panel, aria-expanded="false" on trigger. Disabled: disabled (or aria-disabled="true") on trigger. Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" on trigger (native rule is :focus-visible:not(:focus), never matches); hover works natively. Item gets data-hide-separator="true" (hides separator) when Root hideSeparator is set. Toggle/animation/single-vs-multiple expansion are RAC runtime.
Accordion.openQuestions: partDetails lists no part for accordion__body-inner (auto-rendered inside Body).

Alert.notes: DOM: div.alert.alert--<status>[data-slot=alert-root] (React adds NO role/aria; add role="alert" yourself if wanted) > div.alert__indicator[data-slot=alert-indicator] > svg[data-slot=alert-default-icon], then div.alert__content[data-slot=alert-content] > p.alert__title[data-slot=alert-title] + span.alert__description[data-slot=alert-description]. The data-slot=alert-default-icon is on the svg, not the indicator div: CSS .alert__indicator [data-slot=alert-default-icon] sizes it to 16px content-box, so a custom icon needs that data-slot to get the same sizing. Injected default icon per status (all 16x16 viewBox, fill none, path fill=currentColor, aria-hidden=true, role=presentation; source icons.js): default -> InfoIcon (circle with i), accent -> InfoIcon, success -> SuccessIcon (circle with check), warning -> WarningIcon (triangle with !), danger -> DangerIcon (circle with !). Indicator/title color come from descendant selectors .alert--<status> .alert__indicator / .alert__title (no data attributes). status is a Root prop only (default "default"); no state attributes. Alert also provides SurfaceContext {variant:"default"} (unread, nothing to author).
Alert.openQuestions: generatorDraft.partDetails.Indicator.dataSlot is alert-default-icon, but the indicator div's own data-slot is alert-indicator; alert-default-icon belongs to the svg child.

AlertDialog.notes:
Same overlay structure as Modal: .alert-dialog__backdrop > .alert-dialog__container > section.alert-dialog__dialog[role=alertdialog][tabindex=-1][aria-labelledby=] > .alert-dialog__header (> .alert-dialog__icon, h2.alert-dialog__heading[slot=title][id]), .alert-dialog__body, .alert-dialog__footer; parts carry data-slot=alert-dialog-. Trigger = div.alert-dialog__trigger[role=button][tabindex=0] (aria-expanded/aria-controls/id as for Modal). Differences from Modal: role=alertdialog; no scroll prop, no size full, no container modifier classes, no modal__icon; dialog is max-h-full overflow-clip and body is always overflow-y-auto. Put style="--visual-viewport-height:100dvh" on the backdrop (backdrop/container height depend on it, see Modal). data-placement (auto default | top | center | bottom) must be on BOTH container and dialog. size is a Container prop but its class lands on the Dialog via context (default md: write alert-dialog__dialog--md). variant is on Backdrop; status is on Icon, not on the root. Icon markup:
; the svg MUST carry data-slot=alert-dialog-default-icon (CSS box-content size-5). Default svg by status: default and accent = HeroUI Info icon, success = check-circle, warning = triangle-exclamation, danger (default status) = circle-exclamation; custom children replace it. Backdrop defaults isDismissable=false and keyboard dismiss disabled (behavior only). CloseTrigger: same CloseButton markup as Modal with class alert-dialog__close-trigger and data-slot=alert-dialog-close-trigger. The CSS rule .alert-dialog__header > .modal__icon is stale (never matches). data-entering/data-exiting on backdrop/container are animation-only (omit). Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true".

Filter.why: RAC Autocomplete wrapper: no own DOM, renders children only

Autocomplete.notes: Built from RAC Select + Autocomplete filter (searchable select). Root: div.autocomplete.autocomplete--<primary|secondary>[.autocomplete--full-width][data-slot=autocomplete] (flex flex-col gap-1; Label/Description/FieldError as in Select; root data-invalid="true" or aria-invalid="true" drives the invalid trigger style). Trigger is NOT a button: div.autocomplete__trigger[.autocomplete__trigger--full-width][role=group][data-slot=autocomplete-trigger] (RAC Group; data-hovered/data-focus-visible/data-focus-within/data-disabled/data-invalid; disabled = data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true", :disabled cannot match a div; focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true") holding span.autocomplete__value[data-slot=autocomplete-value][data-placeholder=true when empty], optional ClearButton, and Indicator. ClearButton: <button aria-label="Clear selection" class=autocomplete__clear-button data-slot=autocomplete-clear-button data-empty="true" [disabled]> with svg[data-slot=autocomplete-clear-button-icon] (Close icon, viewBox "0 0 16 16"; the data-slot is required, CSS size-3.5); data-empty="true" = nothing selected -> opacity 0 + pointer-events none (omit the attribute to show it). Indicator default: <button type=button aria-haspopup=listbox aria-expanded> (RAC Button consuming the Select trigger context; no HeroUI classes) wrapping svg.autocomplete__indicator[data-slot=autocomplete-default-indicator][data-open=true when open -> rotate 180deg] chevron-down 16x16 (absolute end-2; trigger pe-7 via :has(.autocomplete__indicator)); a custom child gets data-slot=autocomplete-indicator. Popover (portaled): div.autocomplete__popover[data-slot=autocomplete-popover][data-placement=bottom] with RAC inline position:absolute; z-index:100000; top/left/max-height; --trigger-anchor-point, plus React inline --trigger-width:<trigger offsetWidth px> (CSS w and max-w = var(--trigger-width), pt-2, overflow-hidden: set it). It auto-renders an inner section.autocomplete__popover-dialog[role=dialog][data-slot=autocomplete-popover-dialog][tabindex=-1] (no separate public part; the popover itself then has no role) holding the author content: a SearchField (root must carry data-slot=search-field: px-3 py-1), a ListBox (data-slot=list-box: max-h-[320px] overflow-y-auto p-1.5; items need data-slot=list-box-item; aria-multiselectable=true on the listbox for multi-select), and an optional empty-state element data-slot=empty-state (text-center text-sm). Autocomplete.Filter renders NO DOM (RAC filter wrapper); autocomplete__filter exists in the tv slots but is never emitted and has no CSS. Selected item look: see ListBoxItem (aria-selected + checkmark dashoffset 44).
Autocomplete.openQuestions: autocomplete__popover-dialog has no part entry; documented as an implicit inner element of Popover.

propTargets.color: Fallback (class avatar__fallback--<color>; set on Root it is forwarded to the fallback slot, Fallback accepts its own color override)

Avatar.notes: DOM: span.avatar[.avatar--sm|--lg][.avatar--soft] (Radix AvatarPrimitive.Root renders a span; HeroUI sets no data-slot on root or image) containing img.avatar__image[src][alt] and/or span.avatar__fallback.avatar__fallback--[data-slot=avatar-fallback] with initials/icon. No data-* or state attribute selects between image and fallback: Radix mounts the only after the image has loaded and renders the fallback only while it has NOT loaded (React never shows both). In static HTML include the one you want; if you include both, the absolutely positioned img (inset 0, size-full, aspect-square) covers the fallback once it loads, and a failed load shows the browser's broken-image box over it. The fallback ALWAYS carries a color class (React default avatar__fallback--default); color is read from Root (tv) and Fallback also accepts its own color override, but the class goes on the FALLBACK element, never on .avatar. variant=soft (avatar--soft on root) makes root bg transparent and gives the fallback a tinted bg per color class (avatar--soft .avatar__fallback--). avatar--lg also bumps fallback text to text-base via descendant selector; avatar--md is inert.

Anchor.why: Hardcoded cx("badge-anchor") in React; block listed as extraBlock

Badge.notes: Static markup: 3. React always emits a placement class (default badge--top-right), and every placement class is position:absolute with a +-25% translate, so a .badge must sit inside span.badge-anchor (position:relative; inline-flex; class hardcoded in React, no variants) as a sibling AFTER the host element, or inside another positioned ancestor. Omitting the placement class gives an in-flow inline badge (CSS allows it; React never produces it). Default emitted classes: badge badge--default badge--primary badge--top-right (badge--md and badge--secondary are inert no-op classes). Dot badge: leave .badge empty (min-h/min-w: 28px md, 32px lg, 16px sm). String/number children are auto-wrapped in span.badge__label; other children are not, wrap text manually. Ring around the badge is border: 1px solid var(--badge-border) (= var(--background)). No state attributes.

Item.why: Renders li.breadcrumbs__item containing a.breadcrumbs__link plus a separator span.breadcrumbs__separator (chevron svg) unless last item

Breadcrumbs.notes: DOM: ol.breadcrumbs[data-slot=breadcrumbs][aria-label="Breadcrumbs"] (RAC default, en-US string, localized by RAC; it renders an <ol>, not a nav, so wrap it yourself if wanted) > li.breadcrumbs__item[data-slot=breadcrumbs-item]* , each containing a.link.breadcrumbs__link (React renders the HeroUI Link inside, so the anchor carries BOTH classes "link breadcrumbs__link") followed, for every item except the last, by the injected separator svg.breadcrumbs__separator[data-slot=breadcrumbs-separator][aria-hidden=true] (default 16x16 chevron-right svg, sized size-3, rotate-180 under rtl) as a SIBLING of the link inside the li. LAST (current) item: li gets data-current="true" and data-disabled="true"; its link is rendered as <span role="link" class="link breadcrumbs__link" aria-current="page" aria-disabled="true" data-current="true" data-disabled="true"> (a span, not an a) with NO separator. The CSS keys on data-current="true" on the LINK (text-link color, opacity 100; without it the aria-disabled rule from .link would dim it). Hover underline works natively (data-hovered forces). separator is a Root prop applied to every Item via context: a custom element separator gets class breadcrumbs__separator + data-slot added (cloneElement); a plain string/text separator gets no class. Part 'Item' is the li; Link and Separator are auto-rendered children, not separate parts.

ButtonGroup.notes:
Static markup:
containing .button children (RAC Group adds role=group and data-disabled / data-hovered / data-focus-within / data-focus-visible; CSS uses none of them). The orientation class is always emitted (default horizontal). size and variant are NOT classes on the group. Cascade in React: ButtonGroupRoot clones every DIRECT child with the private prop __button_group_child (BUTTON_GROUP_CHILD); only such Buttons read ButtonGroupContext {size, variant, isDisabled, fullWidth} (their own props win). Static HTML has no context: put button--{variant}, button--sm|--lg, disabled and button--full-width on EACH .button (fullWidth also requires button--full-width per button for equal widths; the group class only sets w-full). CSS is structural: .button-group .button gets radius 0, only .button:first-child / :last-child get the outer radius, .button--outline neighbors drop shared borders, pressed scale is removed and the focus ring is inset; keep buttons as first/last children. Separator: : CSS is position:absolute (horizontal left:-1px;top:25%;width:1px;height:50%; vertical top:-1px;left:25%;width:50%;height:1px; bg currentColor, 15% opacity). The group is not positioned but .button is position:relative, so put it as the first child INSIDE each non-first .button (inferred from CSS; no example found in frontend-alpha); as a direct group child it would anchor to the wrong ancestor and break :last-child. separator__container/__line/__content selectors in separator.css are never emitted by React (the Separator component emits only separator, separator--orientation, separator--variant); button-group uses its own button-group__separator.
ButtonGroup.openQuestions: Separator placement inside the next button is inferred from CSS only; confirm against HeroUI docs. Orientation is read from RAC ToggleButtonGroupContext when the prop is absent (runtime only).

propTargets.visibleDuration: Root (adds literal class calendar--week-view / calendar--day-view; JS only otherwise)
propTargets.isYearPickerOpen: Root prop, but its effect is data-open='true' on YearPickerTrigger and YearPickerGrid (children)

Calendar.notes: DOM (RAC month grid): div.calendar[data-slot=calendar][role=application] > header.calendar__header (button.calendar__nav-button[slot=previous|next][aria-label][data-slot=calendar-nav-button] x2 + h2.calendar__heading[aria-hidden=true] with month-year text, or a year-picker trigger in place of the heading) then table.calendar__grid[role=grid][data-slot=calendar-grid] > thead.calendar__grid-header[aria-hidden=true] > tr > th.calendar__header-cell x7 (weekday text; weekdayStyle is a Grid prop, default 'short'); tbody.calendar__grid-body > tr > td[role=gridcell] > div.calendar__cell[role=button][tabindex]. Only data-slot='calendar-grid' is selected by CSS (year picker); other parts use their class name as data-slot. IMPORTANT: .calendar__cell is on the INNER div, not the td. td and tr carry no class (calendar__grid-row is a tv slot React never emits; CSS targets '> tr' and 'td'). td gets aria-disabled='true' for non-selectable dates (disabled, unavailable, outside-month) and aria-selected='true' for selected. In day view (visibleDuration.days >= 7) blank slots are bare . STATE on div.calendar__cell (value 'true'): data-selected, data-today, data-outside-month, data-unavailable, data-disabled (a div is never :disabled, so the attribute is required). :hover/:active work natively (data-hovered/data-pressed only force). Focus ring: ':focus-visible:not(:focus)' can never match, so ONLY data-focus-visible='true' shows a ring. React gives outside-month cells data-outside-month AND data-disabled (RAC treats them as disabled; the disabled rule excludes them, so no strike-through) and never data-selected, so the [data-selected][data-outside-month] rule never fires. aria-readonly='true' on the table disables cell pointer events. INJECTED: nav icon (default when no children): svg.calendar__nav-button-icon[data-slot=calendar-nav-button-icon][aria-hidden=true][role=presentation] width/height 16, viewBox 0 0 16 16, fill none, path fill=currentColor fill-rule=evenodd, d previous='M10.53 2.97a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.06L6.56 8l3.97 3.97a.75.75 0 1 1-1.06 1.06l-4.5-4.5a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.06l4.5-4.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0' next='M5.47 2.97a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0l4.5 4.5a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.06l-4.5 4.5a.75.75 0 1 1-1.06-1.06L9.44 8 5.47 4.03a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.06Z'. Cell content = day number (custom children replace it). Optional dot: span.calendar__cell-indicator[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=calendar-cell-indicator] as DIRECT child of the cell (accent-foreground only when the cell has data-selected='true'). LITERAL CLASSES calendar--week-view (visibleDuration.weeks) / calendar--day-view (visibleDuration.days) are plain strings React appends to root, not tv variants: add by hand. Year-picker parts: see CalendarYearPicker.
Calendar.openQuestions: YearPickerGridBody is a React Fragment that maps years to Cells and emits no element, so partFixes sets it to null. Year-grid top/height numbers (CalendarYearPicker) are derived from CSS, not measured.

CalendarYearPicker.blockNote: No element carries this block class: calendar-year-picker is only the prefix of its parts (trigger, year-grid, year-cell, ...), which live inside .calendar / .range-calendar.

propTargets.isYearPickerOpen: Parent Calendar/RangeCalendar Root (not a CalendarYearPicker prop); effect is data-open on Trigger and Grid

CalendarYearPicker.notes:
Not standalone: parts live inside .calendar or .range-calendar. CSS structure requirements: (1) the day-grid table must be a DIRECT child of the calendar root with data-slot='calendar-grid' (RangeCalendar: 'range-calendar-grid'), since '.calendar:has(.calendar-year-picker__year-grid) > [data-slot=calendar-grid]' fades it out; (2) the year grid div is a sibling of that table in the same root (root becomes position:relative via :has); (3) the trigger must sit inside .calendar__header / .range-calendar__header (the header hides nav buttons via :has(.calendar-year-picker__trigger[data-open=true])).
OPEN STATE: data-open='true' on BOTH button.calendar-year-picker__trigger (plus aria-expanded='true') and div.calendar-year-picker__year-grid. Closed = omit data-open (CSS only matches 'true'; React emits aria-expanded='false').
TRIGGER: button[type=button].calendar-year-picker__trigger[data-slot=calendar-year-picker-trigger][aria-expanded][aria-label='<Month Year>, year selector'] > span.calendar-year-picker__trigger-heading (month-year text) + span.calendar-year-picker__trigger-indicator[aria-hidden=true] whose default child is the chevron-right svg (height/width 1em, viewBox 0 0 16 16, path as Calendar 'next'). Open: indicator rotates 90deg, heading takes accent colour.
YEAR GRID: div.calendar-year-picker__year-grid[role=listbox][tabindex=-1][aria-hidden=true|false][data-slot=calendar-year-picker-grid]. CSS gives absolute, left/right 0, 3 columns, overflow-y auto, opacity 0 + pointer-events none until data-open. React writes INLINE style top:Npx; height:Npx (JS copies the day grid's offsetTop/offsetHeight); static HTML must hardcode them: top about 40px (24px nav button + 16px header pb-4), height about 28px + 36px per week row at the fixed 252px width (derived from CSS, unverified).
CELL: button[type=button].calendar-year-picker__year-cell[data-slot=calendar-year-picker-year-cell][data-year=2026][aria-label=2026][aria-selected=true|false][tabindex=-1; the active year gets 0 while open] with the year text. Selected: data-selected='true' (aria-selected='true' is styled too); hover via :hover (hover+fine pointer) or data-hovered='true'; native :focus-visible works.
GridBody renders NO element (Fragment mapping years to Cells), so it has no class. Default year list spans minValue..maxValue (1900-2099) unless visibleYears is set; static markup lists any years. isYearPickerOpen / defaultYearPickerOpen are props of the Calendar/RangeCalendar root.
CalendarYearPicker.openQuestions: Hardcoded top/height values for the year grid are derived from CSS sizes (nav button size-6, header pb-4, header cell pb-2 text-xs, td mt-1 on first row, 36px cells at 252px width), not measured.

Card.notes: DOM: div.card.card--<variant>[data-slot=card] > div.card__header[data-slot=card-header] (flex-col wrapper for the title/description) > h3.card__title[data-slot=card-title] + p.card__description[data-slot=card-description]; div.card__content[data-slot=card-content] (flex-1 flex-col gap-1); div.card__footer[data-slot=card-footer] (flex-row items-center). All parts optional; layout is DOM order inside the flex-col gap-3 root. variant defaults to "default" in the component, so React always emits card--default when omitted (transparent = no bg/shadow). Card provides SurfaceContext {variant} to descendants unless variant is transparent, but no component in @heroui/react 3.2.1 reads it (grep-verified), so nothing to reproduce statically. No state attributes, no injected children.

isSelected.target: Root (.checkbox); also pair with svg stroke-dashoffset=44

propTargets.variant: Root (checkbox--secondary on .checkbox); when absent, inherited from CheckboxGroup via CheckboxGroupContext

Checkbox.notes: DOM React renders: div.checkbox[data-slot=checkbox] > label.checkbox__content[data-slot=checkbox-content] (RAC CheckboxButton) > [hidden-input span] + span.checkbox__control[data-slot=checkbox-control] > span.checkbox__indicator[data-slot=checkbox-indicator][aria-hidden=true] > svg; the Label (class="label" data-slot="label") sits inside the content label. Hidden input (optional for CSS): RAC VisuallyHidden span (inline 1px clip-rect style) wrapping <input type="checkbox"> as first child of the content label. Description / FieldError are DIRECT children of .checkbox, after the content label: <span class="description" data-slot="description">, <span class="field-error" data-slot="field-error" data-visible="true"> (CSS .checkbox > [data-slot=description|field-error], ps-7; field-error is forced visible and text-muted here). STATE goes on the ROOT .checkbox: data-selected="true", data-indeterminate="true", data-invalid="true", data-disabled="true". React never sets aria-checked/aria-invalid on the root (they live on the hidden input); checkbox--disabled is CSS-only (React uses data-disabled on root). No :has(input:checked) fallback for checkbox. data-hovered / data-pressed / data-focus-visible are set by RAC on the CONTENT label: force them on [data-slot=checkbox-content]. Native .checkbox:hover/:active work; focus ring needs data-focus-visible="true" on the content label (root div never focuses). INJECTED SVG (one, chosen by state, inside the indicator): checkmark <svg data-slot="checkbox-default-indicator--checkmark" aria-hidden="true" role="presentation" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" viewBox="0 0 17 18" stroke-dasharray="22" stroke-dashoffset="66"><polyline points="1 9 7 14 15 4"/></svg>. The tick is drawn by the stroke-dashoffset ATTRIBUTE (66 hidden, 44 visible), not by CSS (CSS only transitions it): selected static = data-selected="true" on root AND stroke-dashoffset="44". Indeterminate (replaces the checkmark; data-indeterminate="true" on root): <svg data-slot="checkbox-default-indicator--indeterminate" aria-hidden="true" role="presentation" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><line x1="21" x2="3" y1="12" y2="12"/></svg>. Required star: data-required="true" is set on the content label, so a direct-child .label gets the asterisk (selector analysis); or use label--required.
Checkbox.openQuestions: generatorDraft partDetails.Indicator.dataSlot (checkbox-default-indicator--indeterminate) is misleading: the indicator span's own data-slot is checkbox-indicator; the --checkmark/--indeterminate values are on the inner svg. BEM mapping (checkbox__indicator) is correct, no partFix. Required star: label.css comment says option labels should be excluded, but the selector keys on the root data-slot (radio/checkbox), not on the content label, so a required Checkbox label does get the asterisk.

isInvalid.target: Root (.checkbox-group); items need their own data-invalid

isDisabled.target: Root (.checkbox-group); items need their own data-disabled

propTargets.variant: Root class is inert (no CSS); real effect cascades via CheckboxGroupContext to each Checkbox as checkbox--secondary

CheckboxGroup.notes: Root: <div class="checkbox-group" data-slot="checkbox-group" role="group"> (RAC adds role=group + aria-labelledby; React never emits role=checkboxgroup although label.css selects it). Children in order: group Label <span class="label" data-slot="label"> (RAC context forces a span here), optional <span class="description" data-slot="description">, group-level <span class="field-error" data-slot="field-error" data-visible="true"> (checkboxes inside a group render no FieldError of their own), then the .checkbox items. CSS: .checkbox-group [data-slot=checkbox] {margin-top:1rem}, so every item root must carry data-slot="checkbox" for spacing. RAC sets data-invalid / data-disabled / data-readonly / data-required = "true" on the group; CSS reacts indirectly: [data-invalid=true] .label turns all descendant labels red, [data-disabled=true] .label dims them, [data-required=true] > .label adds the asterisk to a direct-child label. variant: React emits checkbox-group--primary|--secondary on the group but NO CSS exists for either class. The real effect is context: each Checkbox without its own variant renders checkbox--secondary, so for a secondary group the author must add checkbox--secondary to every .checkbox item by hand. isDisabled/isInvalid/isRequired also flow by RAC state to items: set data-disabled="true" / data-invalid="true" on each item root yourself.
CheckboxGroup.openQuestions: checkbox-group--primary / --secondary are emitted by React but have no CSS rule; confirm the kit should treat them as inert.

Chip.notes: Static markup: Text. React default classes: chip chip--default chip--secondary (chip--secondary has no CSS); size has no default, so no size class unless set (chip--md only repeats base text-xs; sm/lg change padding/text). Auto-wrap: if children is a plain string or number React wraps it in span.chip__label; any other children (icon + text, elements) are NOT wrapped, so wrap the text yourself. Icons: place svg directly inside .chip (no svg sizing rule exists, set width/height yourself). Chip is non-interactive: no state attributes, no hover/focus rules. Colors come from compound selectors: --primary has solid bg only for accent/success/warning/danger (chip--primary.chip--default has no compound rule and looks like secondary); --soft has compounds for all five colors; --tertiary makes bg transparent.

CloseButton.notes: Static markup: <button type="button" class="close-button close-button--default" data-slot="close-button" aria-label="Close"><svg data-slot="close-button-icon" aria-hidden="true" role="presentation" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none"><path fill="currentColor" fill-rule="evenodd" clip-rule="evenodd" d="(X shape)"/></svg></button>. React injects the CloseIcon svg (16x16, single X path, fill=currentColor, data-slot="close-button-icon") when no children are given, and aria-label="Close"; the author writes both. React always emits close-button--default, which supplies bg-default, text-muted and the hover/pressed colors; a bare .close-button has no background or color. States: native :hover (hover:hover media) and :active (scale .93) or data-hovered / data-pressed = "true"; disabled via disabled / aria-disabled="true"; data-pending="true" (pointer-events:none; RAC also sets aria-disabled while pending); focus ring only with data-focus-visible="true" (native selector :focus-visible:not(:focus) cannot match). Any svg child is forced to size-4. In SearchField the clear button is a CloseButton with extra class search-field__clear-button (size-5, mr-2, icon shrinks to size-3), data-slot overridden to search-field-clear-button and slot="clear".

ColorArea.notes:
DOM: div.color-area[data-slot=color-area][role=group][aria-label] > div.color-area__thumb[data-slot=color-area-thumb][role=presentation]. RAC also puts two visually-hidden input[type=range] (x then y channel) inside the thumb; only needed for interactivity, not visuals.
INLINE STYLES / CSS VARS (CSS reads these, never declares them): on the ROOT --color-area-background = the full CSS gradient (CSS rule is 'background: var(--color-area-background)'; RAC also writes the same gradient as inline background plus position:relative, touch-action:none, forced-color-adjust:none); on the THUMB --color-area-thumb-color = the currently selected colour as a CSS colour (CSS background-color:var(...); RAC also writes inline background-color). Gradient for HSB with x=saturation, y=brightness at hue H (derived from RAC useColorAreaGradient): 'linear-gradient(to top, #000, transparent), linear-gradient(to right, #fff, transparent), hsl(H 100% 50%)'. For colorSpace=rgb RAC instead layers per-channel gradients and sets inline background-blend-mode:screen, which no CSS provides.
THUMB POSITION is inline only: .color-area__thumb has no position in CSS (only size-4, 3px white border, rounded). Author must write style='position:absolute; left:X%; top:Y%; transform:translate(-50%,-50%)' with X = x-channel fraction*100 and Y = (1 - y-channel fraction)*100 (RAC useColorAreaState.getThumbPosition; X mirrored in RTL). Root already has position:relative, aspect-ratio 1, max-w-56, inset 1px shadow.
STATE: data-focus-visible='true' on thumb (no native pseudo rule; ring only via attribute); data-dragging='true' on thumb (grows to size-5); data-disabled='true' on root (and thumb) for disabled. showDots (Root prop) = class color-area--show-dots (::after dot overlay; no extra element).
ColorArea.openQuestions: Exact CSS colour string RAC writes for the thumb (getDisplayColor().toString()) was not verified; any valid CSS colour of the current value works.

propTargets.fullWidth: Root (color-field--full-width); Group has its own fullWidth -> color-input-group--full-width
propTargets.variant: Group (ColorInputGroup root, color-input-group--secondary); not a ColorField root prop

ColorField.notes:
Thin wrapper: Root = RAC ColorField div.color-field[data-slot=color-field][data-channel=hex|<channel>] (flex column gap-1); only prop fullWidth (color-field--full-width). Field visuals come from the Group = ColorInputGroup (classes color-input-group*; ColorField.Group/Input/Prefix/Suffix are re-exports of the ColorInputGroup parts), see ColorInputGroup notes. Inside ColorField RAC gives the Group role='presentation' and passes isInvalid/isDisabled to it (-> data-invalid / data-disabled on the group).
Root children: Label (data-slot='label'), the Group, Description (data-slot='description', hidden by CSS when ROOT has data-invalid='true' or aria-invalid='true'), FieldError. Root attrs from RAC: data-invalid, data-disabled, data-readonly, data-required. Static invalid field: data-invalid='true' on root AND on .color-input-group. Minimal: div.color-field > span[data-slot=label] + div.color-input-group > input.color-input-group__input[data-slot=color-input-group-input][value='#0485F7']. With the channel prop React also renders a hidden form input (not needed for CSS). variant / group-level fullWidth belong to the Group part.

ColorInputGroup.notes:
Root = RAC Group: div.color-input-group[role=group (presentation when inside ColorField)][data-slot=color-input-group] (inline-flex, h-9, bordered). Children in order: optional div.color-input-group__prefix[data-slot=color-input-group-prefix] (usually holds a .color-swatch, see ColorSwatch), input[type=text].color-input-group__input[data-slot=color-input-group-input] (hex text), optional div.color-input-group__suffix[data-slot=color-input-group-suffix]. data-slot values are LOAD-BEARING: ':has([data-slot=color-input-group-prefix|suffix])' removes input side radius and tightens padding; '.color-input-group--secondary [data-slot=color-input-group-input]' makes the input transparent. Unlike date-input-group, prefix/suffix have NO pointer-events:none.
STATE: group data-invalid='true' (danger outline + border colour), data-disabled='true' or aria-disabled='true' (status-disabled on the group; also set disabled on the input). :hover and :focus-within are native (data-hovered / data-focus-within only force them). The input itself needs no state attrs.
CSS GAP: invalid rule reads var(--color-field-border-invalid), which is never declared in @heroui/styles dist; declare it on :root (e.g. var(--danger)) or the invalid border colour likely computes to currentcolor. Props variant (color-input-group--secondary) and fullWidth (color-input-group--full-width) are on this Root.
ColorInputGroup.openQuestions: Border colour fallback when --color-field-border-invalid is undeclared inferred from CSS spec, not checked in a browser.

ColorPicker.notes: Root: div.color-picker[data-slot=color-picker] (inline-flex; RAC ColorPicker and DialogTrigger render no DOM of their own). Trigger: <button type=button class=color-picker__trigger data-slot=color-picker-trigger aria-expanded=false|true> (RAC Button inside DialogTrigger: id, aria-expanded, aria-controls while open, no aria-haspopup; inline-flex items-center gap-3 rounded-sm text-sm), typically containing a ColorSwatch and a Label (class label, data-slot=label; CSS gives it the interactive cursor). Trigger states: disabled via :disabled, data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true"; focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" (:focus-visible:not(:focus) cannot match natively). Popover (portaled): div.color-picker__popover[data-slot=color-picker-popover][data-placement=bottom|top|left|right][role=dialog][tabindex=-1] (flex-col gap-3, min-w-62, overflow-y-auto; default placement prop "bottom left", RAC resolves data-placement to the axis; CSS matches it with ^=) with RAC inline position:absolute; z-index:100000; top/left/max-height px; --trigger-anchor-point (transform-origin only); the author positions it. It holds ColorArea / ColorSlider / ColorField / ColorSwatchPicker children. In React the picker state feeds those children their color via context; statically each child needs its own explicit color styling (see their entries). data-entering/data-exiting="true" only animate. role=dialog inferred from RAC Popover.mjs logic (no nested dialog).
ColorPicker.openQuestions: Child-component color inlining (ColorSwatch --color etc.) belongs to those components' entries and was not verified here.

propTargets.orientation: Root (data-orientation; RAC also sets it on Track/Output but CSS only needs it on Root)

ColorSlider.notes:
DOM: div.color-slider[data-slot=color-slider][data-orientation=horizontal|vertical] > [label[data-slot=label]] + [output.color-slider__output[data-slot=color-slider-output]] + div.color-slider__track[data-slot=color-slider-track] > div.color-slider__thumb[data-slot=color-slider-thumb]. data-orientation on the ROOT is REQUIRED (all track/thumb sizing sits under .color-slider[data-orientation=...]; React defaults it to horizontal). The 3-area grid (label/output/track) collapses via ':has([data-slot=label])' and ':has(.color-slider__output)', so the label needs data-slot='label' and output the class. Label text defaults to the channel name (e.g. Hue); output text = formatted channel value. RAC puts role=group + aria-label on the TRACK and a visually-hidden input[type=range] inside the thumb (interactivity only).
INLINE STYLES (CSS declares none): TRACK style = 'background: linear-gradient(to right, <stops>), repeating-conic-gradient(#efefef 0% 25%, #f7f7f7 0% 50%) 50% / 16px 16px; --track-start-color: <css colour at channel min>; --track-end-color: <css colour at channel max>'. Gradient direction 'to right' (LTR horizontal) or 'to top' (vertical); stops: hue = 7 stops at 0,60,...,360deg; lightness adds a middle stop; saturation/brightness/red/green/blue/alpha = 2 stops (channel min, channel max) with the other channels held at the current value. --track-start-color/--track-end-color drive the 0.625rem ::before/::after edge caps outside the track (start cap = colour over checkerboard; end cap = background-color only); without them caps are transparent. THUMB style = 'left:P%' (horizontal) or 'top:(100-P)%' (vertical), 'transform:translate(-50%,-50%)', and 'background-color:<current colour>' (React omits it when disabled so .color-slider__thumb[data-disabled=true] bg-default shows). CSS supplies position:absolute, top/left:50% on the cross axis, 16px size, 3px white border, shadow. P = (value-min)/(max-min)*100.
STATE: thumb data-dragging='true' (cursor grabbing), data-focus-visible='true' (ring only via attribute), data-disabled='true' on root and thumb; root div also accepts aria-disabled='true' (:disabled never applies to a div). Props: channel and colorSpace are JS-only (they decide gradient/stops); orientation is the data-orientation attribute on Root.
ColorSlider.openQuestions: Output text format per channel (units) is RAC number formatting and was not checked.

ColorSwatch.notes:
Single element, no child parts: div.color-swatch.color-swatch--circle|--square[role=img][aria-roledescription='color swatch'][aria-label='<colour name>'][data-slot=color-swatch]. The base class has NO border-radius: radius comes only from color-swatch--circle / --square (React default shape=circle), so always add one. Size: color-swatch--xs|sm|lg|xl (default md = 32px; color-swatch--md is an inert class).
COLOUR is inline only: style='--color-swatch-current: <any CSS colour>' (React sets it from the colour prop; the CSS background is linear-gradient(var(--color-swatch-current), var(--color-swatch-current)) over a checkerboard so alpha shows; inset 1px black/10% shadow). RAC also writes inline background-color and forced-color-adjust:none, redundant with the var. No state attributes. Props shape and size are on Root.

propTargets.variant: Root (color-swatch-picker--square changes item/swatch radius via descendant selectors)
propTargets.layout: Root (color-swatch-picker--stack = flex-col; layout is not forwarded to RAC)

ColorSwatchPicker.notes:
DOM (RAC ListBox in grid layout): div.color-swatch-picker[role=listbox][aria-label][data-layout=grid][data-slot=color-swatch-picker] > div.color-swatch-picker__item[role=option][aria-selected][data-slot=color-swatch-picker-item][style='--color-swatch-current:<css colour>'] > div.color-swatch-picker__swatch[role=img][aria-roledescription='color swatch'][aria-label='<colour name>'][data-slot=color-swatch-picker-swatch][style='background-color:<css colour>'] + optional span.color-swatch-picker__indicator[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=color-swatch-picker-indicator].
COLOUR WIRING: the Swatch is a RAC ColorSwatch with ONLY class color-swatch-picker__swatch (it does NOT get .color-swatch); the CSS gives it no background, so its colour is the inline background-color RAC writes. --color-swatch-current is set inline on the ITEM and only drives the selected item border-color.
STATE: selected item = data-selected='true' (plus aria-selected='true') on .color-swatch-picker__item: border takes --color-swatch-current, swatch scales to .77, indicator child scales in. data-focus-visible='true' (also :focus-visible natively) and data-disabled='true' on item. Hover on swatch is native (scale 1.1).
INDICATOR (React-injected, author must write): span.color-swatch-picker__indicator (absolute inset-0 centred, pointer-events none) whose CHILD gets the styling (selector '.color-swatch-picker__indicator > *': 1/3 size, white, scale(0), scale(1) when item selected). Default child: svg[data-slot=color-swatch-picker-checkmark][aria-hidden=true][role=presentation] viewBox 0 0 12 12 fill none stroke currentColor stroke-width 1.5 round caps/joins containing polyline points='2.5 6 5 8.5 9.5 3'. Note the span's data-slot is color-swatch-picker-indicator; 'color-swatch-picker-checkmark' is on the inner svg.
CSS BUG: React sets data-light-color='true' on the indicator when luminance>0.5 (to get a black check), but the compiled rule is '.color-swatch-picker__indicator[data-light-color=true] .color-swatch-picker__indicator>*' (self-nested), so it can never match in v3.2.1; the check is always white. Use an inline color:#000 on the svg for light swatches.
Size/shape/layout are Root classes restyling the Item via descendant selectors (color-swatch-picker--xs|sm|lg|xl, --square, --stack); item and swatch carry no modifier classes.

propTargets.fullWidth: Root (also adds combo-box__input-group--full-width on InputGroup via context)
propTargets.variant: Root (cascades through ComboBoxContext to the child Input as input--primary|input--secondary; adds no combo-box class)

ComboBox.notes: Root: div.combo-box[.combo-box--full-width][data-slot=combo-box] (flex flex-col gap-1; RAC adds data-open/data-focused/data-disabled/data-invalid). Children: Label (class label, data-slot=label); div.combo-box__input-group[.combo-box__input-group--full-width][data-slot=combo-box-input-group] (relative isolate inline-flex; a plain div, not a RAC Group); Description/FieldError ([data-slot=description] is hidden when root has data-invalid="true" or aria-invalid="true"). Inside the input group: HeroUI Input = <input class="input input--primary|input--secondary" data-slot=input role=combobox aria-expanded aria-autocomplete=list aria-controls> and ComboBox.Trigger = <button type=button class=combo-box__trigger data-slot=combo-box-trigger tabindex=-1 aria-label="Show suggestions" data-open=true when open>. The input MUST carry data-slot=input: CSS .combo-box [data-slot=input] gives min-w-0 flex-1, focused-field styles on :focus / [data-focus], disabled styles, and pe-7 only when the trigger is its IMMEDIATE next sibling (:has(+ .combo-box__trigger)). The trigger is absolute end-0 top-1/2 h-full; default content svg[data-slot=combo-box-trigger-default-icon] chevron-down 16x16 (size-4; rotates 180deg when the TRIGGER has data-open="true": data-open sits on the button here, not on the svg). Trigger states: :hover/data-hovered, [data-pressed=true] opacity-70, disabled via :disabled, data-disabled or aria-disabled; focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" (:focus-visible:not(:focus) cannot match natively). Popover (portaled): div.combo-box__popover[data-slot=combo-box-popover][data-placement=bottom] with RAC inline position:absolute; z-index:100000; top/left/max-height; --trigger-anchor-point; --trigger-width = pixel width spanning input + trigger button (RAC computes it because no RAC Group is rendered; CSS min-width:var(--trigger-width): set it). No role=dialog (RAC isNonModal). It contains a ListBox (data-slot=list-box -> p-1.5; items need data-slot=list-box-item -> px-2.5; single-select so the checkmark has no transition); selected item = aria-selected + checkmark stroke-dashoffset=44 (see ListBoxItem). Prop menuTrigger defaults to "focus" (behavior only).
ComboBox.openQuestions: ComboBox variant prop is not in generatorDraft.props because the combo-box tv has none; it is only forwarded to Input.

propTargets.fullWidth: Root (date-field--full-width); Group has its own separate fullWidth -> date-input-group--full-width
propTargets.variant: Group (DateInputGroup root, date-input-group--secondary); not a DateField root prop

DateField.notes:
Thin wrapper: Root = RAC DateField div.date-field[data-slot=date-field] (flex column, gap-1); only prop is fullWidth (date-field--full-width). All field visuals come from the Group part = DateInputGroup (classes date-input-group*; DateField.Group/Input/InputContainer/Segment/Prefix/Suffix are re-exports of the DateInputGroup parts), see DateInputGroup notes for DOM, segments and states. Children of the root: Label (element with data-slot='label'; RAC renders it as a span, CSS only sets w-fit via [data-slot=label]), the Group, optional Description (data-slot='description'; hidden by CSS when the ROOT has data-invalid='true' or aria-invalid='true'), FieldError. Root state attrs from RAC: data-invalid, data-disabled, data-readonly, data-required (only data-invalid/aria-invalid matter to CSS; set data-invalid='true' on root AND on the group/segments to render an invalid field). Minimal static:
Birth date
...segments...
. React also renders a hidden form (not needed for CSS). Props not on Root: variant and the group-level fullWidth belong to Group (date-input-group--secondary / --full-width).

DateInputGroup.notes:
Root = RAC Group: div.date-input-group[role=group][data-slot=date-input-group] (inline-flex, h-9, bordered field). Typical children: [div.date-input-group__prefix[data-slot=date-input-group-prefix]] + div.date-input-group__input-container[data-slot=date-input-group-input-container] (scroll wrapper) > div.date-input-group__input[role=group][data-slot=date-input-group-input] > span.date-input-group__segment[data-slot=date-input-group-segment]*, + [div.date-input-group__suffix[data-slot=date-input-group-suffix]]. data-slot values on children are LOAD-BEARING: ':has([data-slot=date-input-group-prefix|suffix])' trims input radius/padding; '.date-input-group--secondary [data-slot=date-input-group-input]' makes the input transparent; the focus ring is suppressed via ':has([data-slot=date-picker-trigger|date-range-picker-trigger]:focus)' so a picker trigger inside must carry that data-slot.
SEGMENTS (RAC DateSegment span): editable = role=spinbutton tabindex=0 contenteditable=true inputmode=numeric aria-label style='caret-color:transparent' data-type=month|day|year|hour|minute|second|dayPeriod|era; literal separators = span aria-hidden=true data-type='literal' (text '/', ':', ' '). Empty segment: data-placeholder='true' with placeholder text (mm/dd/yyyy); filled segment: no attribute. Focused segment styling = :focus (needs tabindex) or data-focused='true'. data-invalid='true' on each segment (red text) and data-disabled='true' (opacity .5).
GROUP STATES: data-invalid='true' (danger outline + border), data-disabled='true' or aria-disabled='true'; :hover and :focus-within work natively (data-hovered / data-focus-within only force them; data-focused unused on the group). Prefix/Suffix are pointer-events:none unless an ancestor .date-picker / .date-range-picker exists (then auto, so the trigger button is clickable).
RANGE: inside DateRangePicker the group holds two inputs; each .date-input-group__input needs attribute slot='start' / slot='end' (React passes slot to the div), and a span.date-range-picker__range-separator sibling; the [slot=start|end] rules (flex:none/pr-0, pl-0) only apply under ':has(.date-range-picker__range-separator)'.
CSS GAP: invalid rule reads var(--color-field-border-invalid), which is not declared anywhere in @heroui/styles dist (only --color-field-border, -hover, -focus exist); declare it on :root (e.g. var(--danger)) or the invalid border-color likely computes to currentcolor. Props variant/fullWidth are on this Root.
DateInputGroup.openQuestions: Border colour fallback when --color-field-border-invalid is undeclared (inferred as currentcolor from CSS spec, not checked in a browser).

propTargets.placement: Popover (only affects entering-animation slide direction via data-placement under data-entering)

DatePicker.notes:
Root = RAC DatePicker div.date-picker[data-slot=date-picker] (inline-flex column gap-1; RAC adds data-open when open, data-invalid/data-disabled/data-focus-within, no CSS on them here). DatePicker has NO input parts of its own: compose Label + DateField.Group (DateInputGroup with segments; see DateInputGroup) + the Trigger inside the group's Suffix + Popover.
TRIGGER: button[type=button].date-picker__trigger[data-slot=date-picker-trigger][aria-haspopup=dialog][aria-expanded][aria-label=Calendar] inside div.date-input-group__suffix; the data-slot value is selected by the DateInputGroup focus-ring rule. Its indicator: span.date-picker__trigger-indicator[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=date-picker-trigger-indicator] whose default child is the calendar icon svg (IconCalendar: width/height 1em, viewBox 0 0 13 14, fill none, one path fill=currentColor evenodd; source in @heroui/react icons.js). Trigger focus ring: only [data-focus-visible=true] works (':focus-visible:not(:focus)' can never match); disabled = :disabled | data-disabled | aria-disabled.
POPOVER: RAC Popover is portaled to <body> (not inside .date-picker): div.date-picker__popover[data-slot=date-picker-popover][role=dialog][tabindex=-1][data-trigger=DatePicker][data-placement=bottom|top|left|right]. RAC sets inline position:absolute; top/left (px); z-index; max-height, plus --trigger-width (px width of the DateInputGroup; CSS min-width) and --trigger-anchor-point ('x y' px; CSS transform-origin). CSS provides none of position/top/left/z-index, so static HTML must set them (position:absolute|fixed, top, left, z-index) and optionally --trigger-width. Content is a .calendar (252px) inside p-3. Enter/exit animations run only with data-entering='true' / data-exiting='true'; slide direction keys on data-placement^=top|bottom|left|right. RAC also adds a transparent fixed underlay and visually-hidden dismiss buttons (not needed).
Props not on Root: placement lives on Popover (default 'bottom'); fullWidth/variant belong to the DateField Group.

propTargets.placement: Popover (only affects entering-animation slide direction via data-placement under data-entering)

DateRangePicker.notes:
Same structure as DatePicker with range-picker classes: Root = div.date-range-picker[data-slot=date-range-picker] (inline-flex column gap-1). Compose Label + DateField.Group + Popover. The group contains TWO inputs: div.date-input-group__input[slot=start] and [slot=end] (each with its own segments), a span.date-range-picker__range-separator[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=date-range-picker-range-separator] between them (default text ' - ' with spaces; px-1, placeholder colour), and a suffix with the trigger. The slot='start'/'end' attributes and the separator class are required for the DateInputGroup ':has(.date-range-picker__range-separator)' rules (start input flex:none pr-0, end pl-0).
TRIGGER: button[type=button].date-range-picker__trigger[data-slot=date-range-picker-trigger][aria-haspopup=dialog][aria-expanded][aria-label=Calendar] inside div.date-input-group__suffix (data-slot value is read by the group focus-ring rule). Indicator span.date-range-picker__trigger-indicator[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=date-range-picker-trigger-indicator] default child = same calendar svg as DatePicker (viewBox 0 0 13 14, 1em). Only [data-focus-visible=true] shows the trigger ring.
POPOVER: portaled to <body>: div.date-range-picker__popover[data-slot=date-range-picker-popover][role=dialog][tabindex=-1][data-trigger=DateRangePicker][data-placement=bottom|top|left|right]; RAC inline: position:absolute; top; left; z-index; max-height; --trigger-width; --trigger-anchor-point. CSS supplies none of position/top/left/z-index, so a static author sets them. Contains a .range-calendar. data-entering='true' / data-exiting='true' trigger the animations; direction from data-placement^=top|bottom|left|right.
Props not on Root: placement on Popover (default 'bottom'). .date-range-picker also sets pointer-events:auto on its .date-input-group__prefix/suffix.

Description.notes: Static markup: <span class="description" data-slot="description"> (RAC Text; React also emits slot="description" and a generated id for aria-describedby; no field CSS selects [slot=description]). Always write both class and data-slot. Placement matters: inside .checkbox / .radio / .switch the rules are direct-child (> [data-slot=description]) so it must be a sibling of the content label, not inside it (indent ps-7 or 3.25rem for switch). In .textfield / .search-field it is hidden (display:none) on any [data-slot=description] descendant when the root has data-invalid="true" or aria-invalid="true"; elsewhere (RadioGroup, CheckboxGroup, Fieldset) only the .description class styles it (text-xs, muted, wrap). Disabled fields dim it via [data-disabled=true] [data-slot=description] (checkbox/radio/switch roots).

Disclosure.notes: DOM: div.disclosure[data-slot=disclosure] (RAC adds data-expanded="true" when open; no CSS keys on it) > h3.disclosure__heading[data-slot=disclosure-heading] (RAC Heading level 3) > button.disclosure__trigger[type=button][slot=trigger][data-slot=disclosure-trigger][id=T][aria-controls=P][aria-expanded=true|false] (inline-block); then div.disclosure__content[data-slot=disclosure-content][id=P][role=group][aria-labelledby=T] (the panel; part 'Content') > div.disclosure__body[data-slot=disclosure-body] (p-2) > div.disclosure__body-inner (auto-added by React; no CSS rule; Body className lands on this inner div). Indicator part (author places it, conventionally inside the trigger after the label): with no children it renders svg.disclosure__indicator[data-slot=disclosure-indicator], the same 16x16 chevron-down svg as Accordion (ml-auto size-4, inherits color); a custom child gets class + data-slot + data-expanded via cloneElement; data-expanded="true" on it rotates -180deg. EXPANDED: data-expanded="true" on .disclosure__content is REQUIRED (opacity:0 otherwise), aria-expanded="true" on trigger; inline style="--disclosure-panel-height:auto" optional (var unset = auto). COLLAPSED: hidden="until-found", aria-hidden="true", style="--disclosure-panel-height:0px", aria-expanded="false". Disabled: disabled or aria-disabled="true" on trigger. Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" on trigger (native :focus-visible:not(:focus) never matches). CSS gap: no .disclosure__heading or .disclosure__body-inner rule exists (disclosure.css defines the flex heading rule as .accordion__heading by mistake), so the heading is a plain block. Toggling is RAC runtime.
Disclosure.openQuestions: disclosure.css/compiled CSS contains `.accordion__heading{display:flex}` instead of `.disclosure__heading`; treat .disclosure__heading and .disclosure__body-inner as classes without CSS rules.

DisclosureGroup.notes: Minimal static markup: div.disclosure-group[data-slot=disclosure-group] wrapping Disclosure blocks (div.disclosure ...). CSS only gives w-full and contain:layout style; no variants, parts or states. RAC DisclosureGroup (a plain div, no role) adds data-disabled when disabled (no CSS) and supplies expansion state to child Disclosures at runtime (expandedKeys, defaultExpandedKeys, allowsMultipleExpanded, isDisabled), so a static author sets each child's data-expanded/aria-expanded/panel markup by hand; only one child open is a runtime rule, not CSS. Accordion does not render this HeroUI component: it renders RAC DisclosureGroup directly with class .accordion.

propTargets.placement: Content (also drives Dialog class drawer__dialog--<placement> via context; data-placement goes on Content and Dialog)
propTargets.variant: Backdrop

Drawer.notes:
Static open markup (same nesting as Modal): .drawer__backdrop[data-slot=drawer-backdrop] > .drawer__content.drawer__content--[data-placement][data-slot=drawer-content] (fixed inset-0 z-50 flex pointer-events-none) > section.drawer__dialog.drawer__dialog--[data-placement][role=dialog][tabindex=-1][aria-labelledby][data-slot=drawer-dialog] > optional .drawer__handle, .drawer__header > h2.drawer__heading[slot=title][id], .drawer__body, .drawer__footer, close trigger. Portaled to . Because Content is a descendant of Backdrop, the backdrop opacity transition (opacity 0 under its data-entering/data-exiting) fades the panel too. placement (default bottom | top | left | right) is a Content prop but must be repeated: Content gets class drawer__content-- AND data-placement; Dialog gets data-placement AND class drawer__dialog-- (context; only --top has CSS, emit all four anyway). Dialog size/radius key on the dialog [data-placement]: bottom/top = w-full max-h-[85vh] with the two outer corners rounded; left/right = h-full w-80 sm:w-96 max-w-[85vw] square. Recommended style="--visual-viewport-height:100dvh" on the backdrop (inherited; CSS h-(--visual-viewport-height) on backdrop and content, both are fixed inset-0 so they still fill the viewport if it is missing). variant is on Backdrop; no size prop. Handle:
; the inner div MUST carry data-slot=drawer-handle-bar (CSS h-1 w-9 bg-separator). Put it first for bottom/left/right (.drawer__handle + header/body mt-0) and last for top (.drawer__dialog--top pb-2, handle pb-0) (inferred from CSS). Trigger is a real
Drawer.openQuestions: Drawer.Backdrop isDismissable (default true) cascades to Dialog through context and only toggles drag handlers (behavior).

Dropdown.blockNote: The root class .dropdown exists in CSS and as a tv slot, but Dropdown (RAC MenuTrigger) renders no DOM and React never applies it; only the dropdown__* parts appear.
Dropdown.notes: Dropdown root is RAC MenuTrigger: renders NO DOM. The .dropdown class (flex flex-col gap-1) exists in CSS and as tv root slot but React never applies it (optional wrapper div). Trigger: Dropdown.Trigger renders <button type=button class=dropdown__trigger data-slot=dropdown-trigger aria-haspopup=true aria-expanded=false|true> (aria-controls while open; id); the usual pattern puts a HeroUI Button directly inside Dropdown instead (no dropdown__trigger class; the CSS comment says the class only shows for a custom trigger). Open popover (React portals to <body>): div.dropdown__popover[data-slot=dropdown-popover][data-placement=bottom|top|left|right][data-trigger=MenuTrigger][role=dialog][tabindex=-1] (RAC inline: position:absolute; z-index:100000; top/left/max-height px; --trigger-anchor-point; --trigger-width unused by CSS; the author positions it) > div.dropdown__menu[role=menu][data-slot=dropdown-menu][aria-labelledby=<trigger id>][data-selection-mode=single|multiple, only when selectionMode is set] > items. The data-slot values are REQUIRED because the CSS selects them: .dropdown__popover [data-slot=dropdown-menu] {p-1.5}, .dropdown__popover [data-slot=menu-item] {px-2.5}, .dropdown__menu [data-slot=separator] {94% wide, centered} (HeroUI Separator carries data-slot=separator). Items = MenuItem entry (div.menu-item[data-slot=menu-item][role=menuitem|menuitemradio|menuitemcheckbox][tabindex=-1]), groups = MenuSection (section.menu-section[role=group] > header.header[data-slot=header]); Dropdown.ItemIndicator and Dropdown.SubmenuIndicator are MenuItem indicators. Submenu: Dropdown.SubmenuTrigger has no DOM; its trigger item needs aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded=true|false, data-has-submenu="true" (+ data-open="true" while open) and a span.menu-item__indicator.menu-item__indicator--submenu[data-slot=submenu-indicator][aria-hidden=true] holding a chevron-right svg; the submenu is a second .dropdown__popover. Trigger states: [data-pressed=true] or :active scale .97; [data-pending=true] pending; disabled = :disabled or [aria-disabled=true]; focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" (:focus-visible:not(:focus) cannot match natively). data-entering/data-exiting="true" only animate. Popover width: max-w-[48svw], md:min-w-55.
Dropdown.openQuestions: Popover role=dialog is inferred from RAC Popover.mjs logic (no nested [role=dialog] => isDialog), not from a DOM capture.

EmptyState.notes:
Minimal static markup:
No results found
. React renders a plain div (no role/aria, no parts, no variants, no state); when children is falsy it renders the default text "No results found", so write the text by hand. Base CSS gives p-2 text-sm text-muted. data-slot="empty-state" is used by CSS only as a context override: .autocomplete__popover [data-slot=empty-state] (text-center, text-sm, overlay-foreground at 60% opacity), so keep the attribute when the element sits inside an autocomplete popover. No HeroUI component in @heroui/react dist imports EmptyState; the autocomplete override suggests it is meant for renderEmptyState in collection components (inference, unverified).

ErrorMessage.notes: Static markup: <span class="error-message" data-slot="error-message"> (RAC Text with slot="errorMessage" also emitted). Always-visible danger text-xs with height:auto: unlike FieldError there is no data-visible gating, and no field container targets [data-slot=error-message] (only tag-group does), so it is not auto-hidden/placed. Validation messages managed by RAC use FieldError; ErrorMessage is for manually shown messages: the author includes it only in the error state. It does not cause the TextField description to hide; set data-invalid on the root for that.

visible.target: Root (.field-error); not a real prop, React hard-codes data-visible=true (presence is what CSS checks)

FieldError.notes: Static markup: <span class="field-error" data-slot="field-error" data-visible="true"> (RAC FieldError -> Text slot="errorMessage"). Visibility is the PRESENCE of data-visible (CSS .field-error[data-visible]); without it the element is height:0 / opacity:0. React hard-codes data-visible="true" and renders the element only when the field is invalid and has content (default content = validation messages joined by a space), so in static HTML include it only in the invalid state. Inside .checkbox / .switch / .radio as a DIRECT child CSS forces it visible (height:auto, opacity 1, no transition) and text-muted (not danger), indented ps-7 (switch 3.25rem). In TextField/SearchField/groups it is danger text-xs with px-1 and a height/opacity transition; those containers also hide their description when data-invalid="true".

Fieldset.notes: Static markup: <fieldset class="fieldset" data-slot="fieldset"> > <legend class="fieldset__legend" data-slot="fieldset-legend">, optional <span class="description" data-slot="description">, <div class="fieldset__field_group" data-slot="fieldset-field-group"> (note single underscore: field_group; children are spaced by :where(> :not(:last-child)) margin-bottom 1rem), <div class="fieldset__actions" data-slot="fieldset-actions"> (flex, gap-2, pt-1). fieldset__description is a tv slot with no React part and zero CSS rules (confirmed by grep): use the generic Description (class description, data-slot description). Disabled: React mirrors a native `disabled` attribute as data-disabled="true" on the fieldset so [data-disabled=true] .label (and similar ancestor selectors) dim descendants; static markup needs BOTH disabled and data-disabled="true". React also forwards isDisabled through RAC contexts (Button, CheckboxGroup, Link, RadioGroup, Slider, ToggleButton, ToggleButtonGroup), so div-based controls get data-disabled; a static author must put data-disabled="true" on those descendants by hand (native inputs/buttons inherit :disabled from the fieldset). No props cascade through classes.
Fieldset.openQuestions: partDetails Group.fn is FieldGroup (exported as Fieldset.Group); BEM mapping fieldset__field_group is correct.

Form.notes: No HeroUI CSS exists for Form (no form.css, no .form rule) and React adds no class or data-slot: FormRoot is a bare RAC Form, i.e. a plain <form> (RAC only adds class react-aria-Form when no className is passed; it sets noValidate unless validationBehavior is native, default native). Static markup: plain <form> with no class; give field spacing yourself (e.g. wrap fields in .fieldset > .fieldset__field_group, or a flex-col gap utility). Runtime-only behavior that static HTML does not reproduce: RAC FormContext/validationErrors that make child fields data-invalid and render FieldError.
Form.openQuestions: generatorDraft block is null: confirm the kit should not map Form to any BEM class.

Header.notes: Minimal static markup: <header class="header" data-slot="header">Label</header>. RAC Header renders a <header> element; HeroUI replaces its className with "header" (w-full px-2 pt-1.5 pb-1 text-left text-xs font-medium text-muted). It is a group/section label meant for RAC collection sections (ListBox/Menu/Select sections, e.g. a section wrapper with the header first) (static section markup unverified). No variants, parts or state attributes.
Header.openQuestions: Static section context for Header (how RAC ListBox/Menu sections wrap it) was not verified.

propTargets.variant: Root (input--secondary); defaults come from TextFieldContext / ComboBoxContext variant

Input.notes: Static markup: <input class="input [input--secondary] [input--full-width]" data-slot="input">. Native :hover, :focus, :disabled work (hover under hover:hover); data-hovered / data-focused / data-focus-visible = "true" force states. Invalid: data-invalid="true" on the input is the only selector (no aria-invalid rule; RAC Input maps aria-invalid to data-invalid at runtime). Disabled: disabled attribute, data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true". variant: when the prop is absent React reads it from TextFieldContext (or ComboBoxContext), so inside a secondary TextField the author must add input--secondary to the input. input--primary is inert. data-slot="input" matters: .textfield--full-width [data-slot=input] widens it. Not the input used by InputGroup (that is .input-group__input / data-slot=input-group-input) nor SearchField (search-field__input). Label/description/error are siblings in the TextField, see TextField.

propTargets.variant: Root (input-group--secondary); inherited from TextFieldContext when absent

InputGroup.notes: Static markup: <div class="input-group [input-group--secondary] [input-group--full-width]" data-slot="input-group" role="group"> (RAC Group; role becomes presentation inside a TextField) containing <div class="input-group__prefix" data-slot="input-group-prefix">, <input class="input-group__input" data-slot="input-group-input"> (or <textarea class="input-group__input" data-slot="input-group-textarea">), <div class="input-group__suffix" data-slot="input-group-suffix">. The data-slot values are functional, not decorative: CSS uses :has([data-slot=input-group-prefix|suffix]) to strip input radius/padding, :has([data-slot=input-group-input|textarea]:focus) for the focus ring, :has([data-slot=input-group-textarea]) for items-start/auto height, [data-slot=input-group-textarea] for resize/min-height, and :autofill. Root state attrs (RAC Group): data-invalid="true" (outline + border + bg), data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true" (dim), data-hovered, data-focus-within, data-focus-visible. Hover has a native :hover fallback; the focus ring is native-only (:has(...:focus)) with no attribute to force it. Root onClick (JS only) focuses the inner input; no CSS. Prefix/suffix are plain divs. Invalid border-color is var(--color-field-border-invalid), a variable declared nowhere (theme defines only --color-field-border, -hover, -focus) and not set by React/RAC: the 1px danger outline still renders, border-color falls back to the initial value (unverified: currentcolor); define --color-field-border-invalid on :root (e.g. var(--danger)) for a red border. variant: root class, or inherited from TextFieldContext when inside a TextField (then add input-group--secondary by hand). Label/description/error are siblings of the group inside .textfield.
InputGroup.openQuestions: --color-field-border-invalid is undeclared in HeroUI 3.2.1 (also used by search-field, number-field, color-input-group, date-input-group). InputGroup isInvalid/isDisabled being accepted as props relies on ...props reaching RAC Group (unverified in d.ts).

propTargets.variant: Root (class input-otp--secondary on the container div; restyles slots via descendant selector)
propTargets.isDisabled: Root (cascades to every Slot via context as data-disabled; not on the container)
propTargets.isInvalid: Root (cascades to every Slot via context as data-invalid)

InputOTP.notes:
Built on the 'input-otp' library, not RAC. Static visuals need only: div.input-otp > div.input-otp__group[data-slot=input-otp-group] > div.input-otp__slot[data-slot=input-otp-slot]* (repeat groups) with div.input-otp__separator[data-slot=input-otp-separator] (6x2px bar) between groups. React container is div.input-otp[data-input-otp-container][style='position:relative;cursor:text;user-select:none;pointer-events:none'] followed by an overlay div[style='position:absolute;inset:0;pointer-events:none'] holding the real input[data-input-otp][data-slot=input-otp][autocomplete=one-time-code][inputmode=numeric][maxlength=N] (class input-otp__input, which has no CSS rule) with a long inline style making it transparent, full-size, font-size:var(--root-height); the lib also injects <style id=input-otp-style>. Only needed for a working field.
SLOT CHILDREN (React-injected): filled slot -> div.input-otp__slot-value[data-slot=input-otp-slot-value] containing the character (plays slot-value-in animation on mount); active AND empty slot -> div.input-otp__caret[data-slot=input-otp-caret] (absolute 2x16px blinking bar, centred by the flex slot).
SLOT STATE attrs (value 'true'): data-active (the focused slot: z-10 + focus ring + field-focus bg), data-filled (has a char: field-focus bg), data-invalid, data-disabled. data-invalid/data-disabled come from Root isInvalid/isDisabled via React context to EVERY slot, so set them on each slot. data-hovered is never set by React and the container has pointer-events:none, so slot :hover never fires in React (static HTML shows :hover natively).
ROOT ATTRS GOTCHA: HeroUI's data-disabled / data-invalid / data-slot='input-otp' land on the hidden <input> (library rest props), NOT on the container, so the rule '.input-otp[data-disabled=true]' (cursor-not-allowed, opacity .5) never matches in React; setting it on the container in static HTML would double-dim with the per-slot data-disabled. variant='secondary' = class input-otp--secondary on the container (className -> container, inputClassName -> input).

propTargets.variant: Root (.kbd)

Kbd.notes: DOM: containing any mix of GLYPH (React Kbd.Abbr keyValue injects the glyph as text and the title) and K for plain key text. React sets NO data-slot on any Kbd part. Variant: tv defaults are empty, so no variant class is emitted by default (kbd--default is an inert class with no CSS); light adds kbd--light (transparent bg). keyValue -> glyph/title: command ⌘ Command, shift ⇧ Shift, ctrl ⌃ Control, option ⌥ Option, alt ⌥ Alt, win ⌘ Win, enter ↵ Enter, delete ⌫ Delete, escape ⎋ Escape, tab ⇥ Tab, capslock ⇪ Caps Lock, up ↑ Up, right → Right, down ↓ Down, left ← Left, pageup ⇞ Page Up, pagedown ⇟ Page Down, home ↖ Home, end ↘ End, help ? Help, space ␣ Space, fn Fn Fn. No states.

Label.notes: Static markup: <label class="label" data-slot="label" for="ID"> (RAC Label default element is label; a <span> when it is the group label of RadioGroup/CheckboxGroup via RAC context; CSS is tag-agnostic). Give EVERY label both class="label" and data-slot="label": field containers style [data-slot=label] (checkbox/radio/switch user-select + cursor, search-field w-fit, etc.) while the typography comes from .label.
