Descendant rules: [data-disabled=true] .label dims (opacity, no pointer events); [data-invalid=true] .label and [aria-invalid=true] .label turn text-danger. Required asterisk (::after "*" in danger): class label--required on the label, OR the label is a DIRECT child (selector uses >) of an element with data-required="true" (union of two selectors: ancestor not role=group|radiogroup|checkboxgroup, or not data-slot=radio|checkbox). React sets data-required on TextField, SearchField, RadioGroup, CheckboxGroup roots and on the content labels of Checkbox/Radio/Switch. label--disabled / label--invalid / label--required classes are only emitted when Label itself receives isDisabled / isInvalid / isRequired; normal React flow relies on ancestor data attributes instead. Position: inside .checkbox__content / .radio__content / .switch__content for toggles; sibling above the control inside .textfield / .search-field / groups.

Link.notes: Static markup: text. RAC renders only when href is set and enabled; otherwise (and aria-disabled="true" when disabled). HeroUI sets NO data-slot on the root. Optional icon after the text: . data-default-icon="true" is set ONLY when the default external-link svg is used (CSS adds ml-1 pb-1.5 to it); omit the attribute when you put your own icon inside link__icon (icon is size 0.75em, opacity 60, 100 on hover/press/focus). Disabled: aria-disabled="true". Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" (native rule is :focus-visible:not(:focus), never matches); hover/pressed work natively (data-hovered/data-pressed force). Combination .link.button drops gap and underline (link styled as button). RAC also emits data-current="true" when aria-current is set (no .link CSS for it; breadcrumbs use it).

propTargets.variant: Root (list-box--danger/--default are emitted but have no CSS)

ListBox.notes: div.list-box[role=listbox][data-slot=list-box][tabindex][aria-label|aria-labelledby][data-layout=stack][data-orientation=vertical][aria-multiselectable=true only for multiple selection] (relative w-full overflow-clip p-1). tv also emits list-box--default / list-box--danger but NO CSS rule exists for either, so the Root variant has no visual effect in 3.2.1. Items, sections and separators must be DIRECT children: spacing is .list-box > * + * {margin-top:.25rem}, not flex gap. Separator needs data-slot=separator AND data-orientation=horizontal (CSS ml 3% / w 94%; vertical not styled); the data-orientation=horizontal in generator stateAttrs belongs to that separator, not to the listbox root. RAC adds data-empty="true" when empty; the empty state is custom content wrapped by RAC in div[role=option] style display:contents (static: write your own). Inside Select/ComboBox/Autocomplete popovers the host block styles the list through [data-slot=list-box] and [data-slot=list-box-item] (padding; max-height in Autocomplete), so those data-slot values are required there. Items = ListBoxItem entry, groups = ListBoxSection. RAC also sets data-focused/data-focus-visible on the root (unstyled).

ListBoxItem.notes: div.list-box-item[role=option][data-slot=list-box-item][tabindex][aria-selected=true|false (RAC writes it whenever selectionMode != none)][data-selection-mode=single|multiple]; tv emits list-box-item--default (no CSS) or list-box-item--danger (variant is a Root prop; danger recolors the indicator and [data-slot=label]). State attrs by hand: disabled = data-disabled="true" (+aria-disabled=true): no :disabled/aria-disabled rule exists; selected = aria-selected="true" or data-selected="true", but the CSS rule for that state is empty, so the only visible selected cue is the Indicator checkmark (stroke-dashoffset); hover (@media hover) / :active have native equivalents (data-hovered, data-pressed to force); focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" (:focus-visible:not(:focus) cannot match natively). Label/description children must carry data-slot=label / data-slot=description (CSS pointer-events none, select-none, w-fit label). Indicator (ListBox.ItemIndicator): span.list-box-item__indicator[data-slot=list-box-item-indicator][aria-hidden=true][data-visible=true when selected; unused by CSS] (absolute end-2 size-4; the item gets pe-7 via :has(.list-box-item__indicator)) > svg[data-slot=list-box-item-indicator--checkmark][viewBox="0 0 17 18"][fill=none][stroke=currentColor][stroke-width=2][stroke-linecap=round][stroke-linejoin=round][stroke-dasharray=22][stroke-dashoffset=66 (unselected, hidden) | 44 (selected, visible)][role=presentation][aria-hidden=true] > polyline points="1 9 7 14 15 4". dasharray/dashoffset are SVG attributes that React sets and the CSS never sets: the author must write them. Inside .select__value and .autocomplete__value the indicator is display:none. The selected-state transition rule in the compiled CSS is mis-nested (.list-box-item__indicator .list-box-item[...]) and never applies.

ListBoxSection.notes: section.list-box-section (flex flex-col items-start gap-0). RAC adds role=group and aria-labelledby=<header id> (or aria-label). First child is the title: <header class="header" data-slot=header role=presentation id=...> (HeroUI Header: w-full px-2 pt-1.5 pb-1 text-left text-xs font-medium text-muted), then the ListBox items as direct children. Spacing between siblings comes from the parent .list-box > * + * margin-top, so keep the section a direct child of .list-box. No props, variants or state attributes.

Menu.notes: Standalone menu (no popover): div.menu[role=menu][data-slot=menu][aria-label|aria-labelledby] (relative flex flex-col gap-1 overflow-clip p-1; RAC adds data-empty="true" when it has no items). Children: Menu.Item (div.menu-item[data-slot=menu-item], see MenuItem), Menu.Section (section.menu-section, see MenuSection), and separators carrying data-slot=separator (CSS .menu [data-slot=separator] {ml 3%; w 94%}). Menu.ItemIndicator = MenuItem indicator. No tv variants/props. selectionMode (none|single|multiple) is a RAC prop with no CSS of its own: it decides item roles (menuitemradio for single, menuitemcheckbox for multiple), aria-checked and data-selection-mode on each item, all written by hand. Inside a dropdown use the Dropdown block instead (class dropdown__menu, data-slot=dropdown-menu), because the .dropdown__popover padding rules key on that data-slot.

propTargets.type: Indicator (checkmark | dot; chooses the svg and data-type, not a class)

MenuItem.notes: Element: div.menu-item[data-slot=menu-item][tabindex=-1][role=menuitem | menuitemradio (parent selectionMode single) | menuitemcheckbox (multiple)]; tv emits menu-item--default (no CSS) or menu-item--danger (variant is a Root prop). Inner label/description must carry data-slot: <span class="label" data-slot=label> and <span class="description" data-slot=description> (CSS: pointer-events none, select-none; danger recolors [data-slot=label]); a Kbd child is also allowed. State attrs by hand: disabled needs data-disabled="true" (+aria-disabled=true): the CSS has no :disabled / aria-disabled rule for menu-item; selected = aria-checked="true" (RAC writes aria-checked on radio/checkbox items) or aria-selected="true" or data-selected="true"; data-selection-mode="multiple" on the item only changes indicator transitions; hover (@media hover) / :active / data-hovered / data-pressed have native equivalents; focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" (:focus-visible:not(:focus) cannot match natively); data-focused and data-open are set by RAC but unstyled. Submenu trigger item: data-has-submenu="true" aria-haspopup=menu aria-expanded=true|false (padding becomes pe-7 ps-2 and any .menu-item__indicator jumps to inline-end). An item holding an indicator gets ps-7 via :has(.menu-item__indicator). Indicator (MenuItem.Indicator / Menu.ItemIndicator / Dropdown.ItemIndicator; prop type = checkmark (default) | dot selects the svg): span.menu-item__indicator[data-slot=menu-item-indicator][data-type=checkmark|dot][aria-hidden=true][data-visible=true when selected; unused by CSS] (absolute start-2, size-4). Checkmark svg: data-slot=menu-item-indicator--checkmark viewBox="0 0 17 18" fill=none stroke=currentColor stroke-width=2 stroke-linecap=round stroke-linejoin=round stroke-dasharray=22 stroke-dashoffset=66 (unselected, hidden) or 44 (selected, visible) role=presentation aria-hidden=true > polyline points="1 9 7 14 15 4". The CSS never sets dasharray/dashoffset: they are SVG attributes React writes, so the author must write them. Dot svg: data-slot=menu-item-indicator--dot viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill=currentColor role=presentation aria-hidden=true > path fill-rule=evenodd clip-rule=evenodd d="M8 15A7 7 0 1 0 8 1a7 7 0 0 0 0 14"; CSS keeps it opacity-0 scale-70 until the item has aria-checked/aria-selected/data-selected="true". SubmenuIndicator (rendered only for items with a submenu): span.menu-item__indicator.menu-item__indicator--submenu[data-slot=submenu-indicator][aria-hidden=true] > chevron-right svg 16x16 (CSS sizes svg to size-3).

MenuSection.notes: section.menu-section (flex flex-col items-start gap-0). RAC adds role=group and aria-labelledby=<header id> (or aria-label). First child is the section title: <header class="header" data-slot=header role=presentation id=...> (HeroUI Header: w-full px-2 pt-1.5 pb-1 text-left text-xs font-medium text-muted); the menu items follow as direct children. Separators between sections are siblings carrying data-slot=separator. A section can take its own selectionMode (RAC), which scopes role/aria-checked of its items. No props, variants or state attributes. Used by both Menu.Section and Dropdown.Section (same component; the class is always menu-section).

propTargets.value: Root props; surface as aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext on root and as inline style width:N% on Fill (Output text defaults to aria-valuetext)
propTargets.minValue: Root (aria-valuemin; used in the Fill width formula)
propTargets.maxValue: Root (aria-valuemax; used in the Fill width formula)

Meter.notes: Root is a div: data-slot="meter", role="meter progressbar" (RAC useMeter), aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin (0), aria-valuemax (100), aria-valuetext (Intl percent of (value-min)/(max-min), e.g. "60%"), plus aria-labelledby=<label id> or aria-label. Children must be DIRECT children of the root (grid areas "label output" / "track track"): label = <span class="label" data-slot="label" id="..."> (CSS selects [data-slot="label"] for grid-area:label; this is the only data-slot the CSS uses; React/RAC forces the label element to span); output = <span class="meter__output" data-slot="meter-output"> (React fills it with aria-valuetext when empty; write the text by hand); track = <div class="meter__track" data-slot="meter-track"> containing <div class="meter__fill" data-slot="meter-fill">. REQUIRED inline style on Fill: style="width:N%" with N = (clamp(value,min,max)-min)/(max-min)*100, unrounded (e.g. 33.333333333333336%). Fill sets no CSS vars; width animates 300ms. Fill colour comes from --meter-fill set by the meter--<color> class on the root. No indeterminate state exists for Meter (no CSS; RAC Meter has no isIndeterminate). Disabled is a CSS-only hook React never emits: set data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true" on the root (opacity .5, pointer-events none).

propTargets.size: Container (class lands on Dialog via context; 'full' also adds modal__container--full on Container)
propTargets.scroll: Container (classes land on Container, Dialog and Body via context)
propTargets.variant: Backdrop

Modal.notes: Static open markup: .modal__backdrop (div) > .modal__container (div) > section.modal__dialog[role=dialog][tabindex=-1][aria-labelledby=<heading id>] > .modal__header > h2.modal__heading[slot=title][id], .modal__body, .modal__footer. React portals them to <body>; the backdrop is position:fixed inset-0 z-50 so it can sit anywhere. Parts carry data-slot=modal-<part> (CSS does not select them). Trigger = div.modal__trigger[role=button][tabindex=0] (Pressable adds tabindex; DialogTrigger adds id, aria-expanded=false|true, aria-controls=<dialog id> while open; no aria-haspopup for dialog type). INLINE VAR: put style="--visual-viewport-height:100dvh" on .modal__backdrop (RAC sets it in px; container inherits it); backdrop and container use h-(--visual-viewport-height), without it the container shrinks to content and data-placement top/bottom and size cover/full break. (RAC also sets --visual-viewport-width/--page-width/--page-height, unused by CSS.) data-placement (auto default | top | center | bottom) must be written on BOTH .modal__container and .modal__dialog; dialog margins key on its own [data-placement] (auto: mt-auto sm:my-auto; center: my-auto; bottom: mt-auto; top: mt-0). size and scroll are Container props but React pushes the classes down via context, so write them on descendants: Dialog gets modal__dialog--<size> and modal__dialog--scroll-<inside|outside>; Body gets modal__body--scroll-<inside|outside>; Container gets modal__container--scroll-outside and, for size full, modal__container--full. Defaults apply even when props are omitted (size md, scroll inside): a default dialog carries modal__dialog--md modal__dialog--scroll-inside and the body carries modal__body--scroll-inside. variant lives on Backdrop (modal__backdrop--opaque default). CloseTrigger = HeroUI CloseButton: <button type=button class="close-button close-button--default modal__close-trigger" aria-label="Close" slot=close data-slot=modal-close-trigger><svg data-slot=close-button-icon viewBox="0 0 16 16" width=16 height=16 fill=none aria-hidden=true role=presentation><path d="M3.47 3.47a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0L8 6.94l3.47-3.47a.75.75 0 1 1 1.06 1.06L9.06 8l3.47 3.47a.75.75 0 1 1-1.06 1.06L8 9.06l-3.47 3.47a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06-1.06L6.94 8 3.47 4.53a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.06Z" fill=currentColor fill-rule=evenodd clip-rule=evenodd/></svg></button>; absolute top-4 right-4 inside the relative dialog. Modal.Icon is a plain div.modal__icon (size-10, flex-centered; no default svg, no color modifiers). data-entering/data-exiting="true" on backdrop/container only drive animation: omit for a static open dialog. Trigger focus ring works only via data-focus-visible="true" (the CSS selector :focus-visible:not(:focus) cannot match natively); pressed via :active or data-pressed. Not reproducible: scroll lock, focus trap, aria-hidden of siblings.
Modal.openQuestions: size/scroll classes land on descendants (Dialog/Body/Container), not only on Container; modifierFor already lists the correct target blocks.

propTargets.fullWidth: Root + Group (number-field--full-width on root, number-field__group--full-width on group; cascades via context)
propTargets.variant: Root (number-field--secondary; styles the group via descendant selector)

NumberField.notes:
DOM: div.number-field[data-slot=number-field] (flex column; RAC data-disabled/data-invalid/data-readonly/data-required) > [label[data-slot=label]] + div.number-field__group[role=group][data-slot=number-field-group] + [description[data-slot=description]] + [FieldError]. The group is display:grid with grid-template-columns:40px 1fr 40px, so DOM order MUST be: decrement button, input, increment button.
BUTTONS: button[type=button][slot=decrement|increment].number-field__decrement-button|increment-button[data-slot=number-field-decrement-button|increment-button][tabindex=-1][aria-label='Decrease|Increase'(+field label, localized)]. The slot attributes are load-bearing: '.number-field__group:has([slot=decrement|increment]) .number-field__input' strips the input's side radius. Default icon children (React-injected; custom children must carry the same data-slot to get size-4): svg[data-slot=number-field-decrement-button-icon|number-field-increment-button-icon][aria-hidden=true][role=presentation] width/height 16 viewBox 0 0 16 16 fill none, path fill=currentColor evenodd; minus d='M1.75 8a.75.75 0 0 1 .75-.75h11a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-11A.75.75 0 0 1 1.75 8'; plus d='M8 1.75a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v4.75h4.75a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5H8.75v4.75a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0V8.75H2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.5h4.75V2.5A.75.75 0 0 1 8 1.75'.
INPUT: input[type=text][inputmode=numeric|decimal|text][aria-roledescription='Number field'].number-field__input[data-slot=number-field-input] (RAC removes role=spinbutton; value is formatted text). STATE: group data-invalid='true' (+ root data-invalid='true' to hide the description), data-disabled='true' or aria-disabled='true' on the group; buttons :active / data-pressed (scale .97), :disabled / data-disabled / aria-disabled. Hover and :focus-within are native on the group (data-hovered / data-focus-within only force them).
CSS GAP: invalid rule reads undeclared var(--color-field-border-invalid) (declare on :root, e.g. var(--danger)).
PROPS: fullWidth on Root yields number-field--full-width on root AND number-field__group--full-width on the group (cascades via React context to the Group): add both classes by hand. variant='secondary' = number-field--secondary on root only (restyles .number-field__group by descendant selector).
NumberField.openQuestions: Hidden form input rendered when name is set (input[type=hidden]) is not needed for CSS.

propTargets.size: Root (nav); children react via descendant selectors, nothing cascades as a class

NextIcon.why: span[data-slot=pagination-next-icon][aria-hidden=true], no BEM class; default child is the chevron-right svg

PreviousIcon.why: span[data-slot=pagination-previous-icon][aria-hidden=true], no BEM class; default child is the chevron-left svg

Pagination.notes: DOM: nav.pagination[data-slot=pagination][role=navigation][aria-label="pagination"] > optional div.pagination__summary[data-slot=pagination-summary] (first child) + ul.pagination__content[data-slot=pagination-content] > li.pagination__item[data-slot=pagination-item] > button.pagination__link[type=button][data-slot=pagination-link]. Ellipsis: span.pagination__ellipsis[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=pagination-ellipsis] with text content "\u2026" (typically inside an li.pagination__item). Current page: data-active="true" AND aria-current="page" on the .pagination__link (data-active has no native equivalent and drives the bg). Previous/Next: React HARDCODES an extra class, so the button is class="pagination__link pagination__link--nav" (data-slot=pagination-previous|pagination-next; no data-active) and contains an injected default (span has no class) followed by the label text; --nav gives w-auto gap-1.5 px-2.5. Disabled: disabled or aria-disabled="true" on the button. Size modifiers pagination--sm|--lg go on the nav only; links, ellipsis and summary are restyled by descendant selectors (no per-child modifier; pagination--md is inert). Hover/active/focus-visible work natively (data-hovered/data-pressed/data-focus-visible force). No page-number logic: the author lays out every page item.
Pagination.openQuestions: Generator parts entry (Next/Previous -> pagination__link) is correct; pagination__link--nav is an additional literal class React always appends (see cssOnlyClasses), so no partFixes.

Arrow.why: No BEM class; CSS targets [data-slot=popover-overlay-arrow] (svg) and [data-slot=popover-overlay-arrow-group] wrapper

Popover.notes:
Static markup: div.popover__trigger[role=button][tabindex=0][data-slot=popover-trigger] (inline-block; React wraps the trigger in it; Pressable adds tabindex, DialogTrigger adds id, aria-expanded and aria-controls while open, no aria-haspopup) and the floating div.popover (the RAC Popover element; React portals it to ) > section.popover__dialog[role=dialog][tabindex=-1][aria-labelledby=][id=][data-slot=popover-dialog] > h2.popover__heading[slot=title][id] (no data-slot) + content. If Popover.Dialog is omitted, RAC puts role=dialog tabindex=-1 on .popover itself. .popover has p-0 (padding comes from .popover__dialog p-4). CSS provides NO positioning: RAC inlines style="position:absolute; z-index:100000; top/left:; max-height:" plus --trigger-anchor-point:"px px" (transform-origin only) and --trigger-width (unused by .popover); the author positions it by hand. Write data-placement=top|bottom|left|right on .popover (RAC-resolved axis; prop default bottom, offset 8): CSS rotates [data-slot=popover-overlay-arrow] by it (bottom 180deg, left -90deg, right 90deg, top 0) and picks the enter slide. RAC also sets data-trigger=DialogTrigger and, for modal popovers, a transparent fixed inset-0 underlay (not needed statically). Optional arrow (Popover.Arrow, only when used):
aria-hidden=true role=presentation style="position:absolute; transform:translateX(-50%) (translateY(-50%) for left/right); :100%; left:px (top:px for left/right)">
; arrow fill comes from CSS keyed on data-slot=popover-overlay-arrow (the svg must carry it); the wrapper has no class. data-entering/data-exiting="true" only drive animation (omit statically). Trigger focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true"; disabled via [aria-disabled=true] or :disabled.
Popover.openQuestions: Heading has no data-slot in React; .popover__heading class is the only hook.

isIndeterminate.note: INVERTED: CSS keys on the attribute being ABSENT. isIndeterminate=true means omit aria-valuenow (and aria-valuetext) on Root and omit the inline width on Fill; false means aria-valuenow=<value> present.

propTargets.value: Root props; surface as aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext on root and as inline style width:N% on Fill (Output text defaults to aria-valuetext)
propTargets.minValue: Root (aria-valuemin; used in the Fill width formula)
propTargets.maxValue: Root (aria-valuemax; used in the Fill width formula)
propTargets.isIndeterminate: Root prop; effect is omitting aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext on root and the width style on Fill

ProgressBar.notes: Root is a div: data-slot="progress-bar", role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin (0), aria-valuemax (100), aria-valuetext (e.g. "60%"), plus aria-labelledby=<label id> or aria-label. DIRECT children of the root (grid "label output" / "track track"): label = <span class="label" data-slot="label" id="..."> (only data-slot the CSS selects); <span class="progress-bar__output" data-slot="progress-bar-output"> (React text defaults to aria-valuetext; write by hand); <div class="progress-bar__track" data-slot="progress-bar-track"> containing <div class="progress-bar__fill" data-slot="progress-bar-fill">. Determinate: Fill needs inline style="width:N%", N = (clamp(value,min,max)-min)/(max-min)*100 (unrounded), and the root MUST carry aria-valuenow. Indeterminate is keyed on the ABSENCE of aria-valuenow: CSS .progress-bar:not([aria-valuenow]) .progress-bar__fill forces width:40% and runs progress-bar-indeterminate 1.5s (translateX -100% to 350%). For a static indeterminate bar omit aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext on the root and omit the width style on Fill (React sets width only when not isIndeterminate; an inline width would override the 40%). A determinate bar missing aria-valuenow animates as indeterminate. Fill colour comes from --progress-bar-fill set by progress-bar--<color> on the root; width animates 300ms. Disabled is a CSS-only hook React never emits: set data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true" on the root.

isIndeterminate.note: INVERTED: CSS keys on the attribute being ABSENT (.progress-circle:not([aria-valuenow]) spins the Track svg). isIndeterminate=true means omit aria-valuenow on Root and use stroke-dashoffset=75.39822368615503 on FillCircle.

propTargets.isIndeterminate: Root prop; effect is omitting aria-valuenow on root and setting FillCircle stroke-dashoffset to C*0.75

ProgressCircle.notes: Root: div data-slot="progress-circle", role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin (0), aria-valuemax (100), aria-valuetext (e.g. "60%"), aria-label (there is no label/output part; root is inline-flex). Children: svg.progress-circle__track (the Track part IS the svg; data-slot="progress-circle-track" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 36 36") containing circle.progress-circle__track-circle (data-slot="progress-circle-track-circle" cx="18" cy="18" r="16" stroke-width="4") and circle.progress-circle__fill-circle (data-slot="progress-circle-fill-circle" cx="18" cy="18" r="16" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" transform="rotate(-90 18 18)" stroke-dasharray=C stroke-dashoffset=OFF). Constants in progress-circle.js: STROKE_WIDTH=4, CENTER=18, RADIUS=CENTER-STROKE_WIDTH/2=16, C=2*PI*16=100.53096491487338. OFF = C - pct/100*C = C*(1-pct/100), pct=(clamp(value,min,max)-min)/(max-min)*100. OFF examples: 0%=100.53096491487338, 25%=75.39822368615503, 50%=50.26548245743669, 60%=40.21238596594935, 75%=25.132741228718345, 100%=0. These are SVG attributes, not inline style or CSS vars. Stroke colours come from CSS vars --progress-circle-stroke / --progress-circle-track-stroke (set by progress-circle--<color>), so the circles need no stroke attribute. Size is set on the svg (md 28px, sm 20px, lg 36px). dashoffset animates 300ms. Indeterminate = ABSENCE of aria-valuenow: CSS .progress-circle:not([aria-valuenow]) .progress-circle__track spins the whole svg (progress-circle-spin 1s linear infinite) and React sets fill-circle dashoffset=C*0.75=75.39822368615503 (a quarter arc); omit aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext. Determinate must keep aria-valuenow. Disabled: data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true" on root (CSS-only hook).

Radio.notes: DOM React renders: root div.radio[data-slot=radio] > label.radio__content[data-slot=radio-content] (RAC RadioButton) > [hidden-input span: same inline-style span as Checkbox but <input type="radio">] + span.radio__control[data-slot=radio-control] > span.radio__indicator[data-slot=radio-indicator][aria-hidden=true], plus Label (class="label" data-slot="label") in the content label. Description / FieldError: direct children of .radio with data-slot="description" / "field-error" (class description / field-error; ps-7). The indicator must be EMPTY (no children, no whitespace): the dot is .radio__indicator:empty::before and any child disables it. Selected: data-selected="true" on the ROOT .radio (CSS uses presence selector [data-selected]); alternatively a real <input type="radio" checked> anywhere inside .radio works via :has(input:checked) (radio only; checkbox/switch have no such fallback). data-invalid="true" and data-disabled="true" also go on the root .radio (React sets them from group state; the aria-invalid/aria-disabled aliases are never emitted; radio--disabled is CSS-only). Radio has NO native :hover/:active/:focus-visible fallback: hover, pressed and focus ring exist only as data-hovered="true", data-pressed="true", data-focus-visible="true" on the content label [data-slot=radio-content] (RAC sets them there). Radio has no variant prop; the secondary look is set by .radio-group--secondary on the RadioGroup. Required star: data-required="true" is set on root and content label when the group is required; a .label that is a direct child of the content label then shows the asterisk (selector analysis); alternative class label--required.
Radio.openQuestions: Selected state is group-driven in React (RadioGroup value); static authors set data-selected on the one chosen .radio. Required star: label.css intends to exclude option labels, but the selector only excludes data-slot=radio/checkbox roots, not the content label, so in a required RadioGroup every option label likely gets an asterisk at runtime (selector analysis, not rendered). Runtime tag of a Label nested in a Radio inside RadioGroup is unverified (RAC LabelContext from the group may make it a span); CSS is tag-agnostic.

propTargets.variant: Root (.radio-group--secondary styles descendant .radio__control; Radio has no own variant)

RadioGroup.notes: Root: <div class="radio-group [radio-group--secondary]" data-slot="radio-group" role="radiogroup" data-orientation="vertical|horizontal">. data-orientation is REQUIRED (React always sets it, default vertical) and there is no orientation class: .radio-group[data-orientation=vertical] [data-slot=radio] {margin-top:1rem}; [data-orientation=horizontal] makes the group a wrapping row with gap-4 (so .radio items need data-slot="radio"). RangeCalendar.notes:
Same skeleton and rules as Calendar with range-calendar* classes/data-slots (range-calendar-header, -nav-button, -grid, -cell, -cell-button, ...). table.range-calendar__grid[role=grid][aria-multiselectable=true][data-slot=range-calendar-grid]; td[role=gridcell] > div.range-calendar__cell[role=button]; tr/td carry no class (range-calendar__grid-row never emitted). Nav buttons use the same chevron svg as Calendar (icon class range-calendar__nav-button-icon).
INJECTED (differs from Calendar): React wraps cell content in span.range-calendar__cell-button[data-slot=range-calendar-cell-button]. CSS styles it as a descendant (circle, today/hover/start/end colours), so the author must write this span inside every cell. The span gets data-selected='true' ONLY on range start/end (isSelectionStart||isSelectionEnd) and data-hovered/pressed/disabled, but no CSS keys on those except the indicator rule '[data-selected=true] > .range-calendar__cell-indicator': put span.range-calendar__cell-indicator[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=range-calendar-cell-indicator] INSIDE the button span.
STATE on div.range-calendar__cell (value 'true'): data-selected on EVERY date in the range incl. endpoints (soft accent track, radius 0); data-selection-start / data-selection-end on the endpoints (accent button, round caps); a one-day range puts both on one cell; data-today, data-outside-month, data-unavailable, data-disabled. Outside-month cells: data-outside-month + data-disabled, never data-selected. :hover/:active native; focus ring only via data-focus-visible='true'.
Row-edge rounding depends on DOM: 'td:first-child > *', 'td:last-child > *', '[aria-disabled] + td > *', 'td:has(+ [aria-disabled]) > *'. The cell must be a direct child of td, and the td of every non-selectable date (disabled, unavailable, outside-month) needs aria-disabled='true'. aria-readonly='true' on the table disables cell pointer events.
LITERAL CLASSES range-calendar--week-view / --day-view added by React to root. Year picker reuses calendar-year-picker__* parts; its crossfade keys on the direct-child table [data-slot=range-calendar-grid] (see CalendarYearPicker). Props not on Root: weekdayStyle on Grid.

ScrollShadow.notes: Single div, no parts or injected children. React sets on the root: data-slot="scroll-shadow", data-orientation=<orientation>, data-scroll-shadow-size=<size> and inline style --scroll-shadow-size:<size>px (default size 40; CSS also defaults the var to 40px, so inline style is only needed when size is not 40). CSS selects none of data-slot, data-orientation, data-scroll-shadow-size (orientation comes from the scroll-shadow--vertical/--horizontal class). The fade is driven only by these attributes, set at runtime by JS via dataset (useScrollShadow: scroll listener + ResizeObserver, in requestAnimationFrame) and matched by CSS ONLY when the value is the string "true": vertical: data-top-scroll (fade on the TOP edge = content hidden above), data-bottom-scroll (fade on the BOTTOM edge = more content below), data-top-bottom-scroll (both); horizontal: data-left-scroll, data-right-scroll, data-left-right-scroll. JS writes top/bottom as "true"|"false" strings, or only data-top-bottom-scroll="true" (deleting the other two) when both apply. Static mock: hard-code ONE attribute, no JS. Scrolled to start with more after: data-bottom-scroll="true" (vertical) / data-right-scroll="true" (horizontal); mid-scroll: data-top-bottom-scroll="true" / data-left-right-scroll="true"; at the end: data-top-scroll="true" / data-left-scroll="true"; no fade: omit all. The fade is a CSS mask, so it renders without real overflow and never updates on scroll in static HTML. CSS gives only position:relative and overflow-y:auto (vertical) / overflow-x:auto (horizontal): the author must constrain height/max-height (vertical) or width/max-width (horizontal) so it scrolls. Scrollbar is excluded from the mask (--scroll-shadow-scrollbar-size 10px; scroll-shadow--hide-scrollbar sets 0px and hides it). React-only props with no CSS effect: isEnabled (default true; disables only the auto JS), offset (px, default 0), onVisibilityChange. visibility (default "auto") "top"|"bottom"|"left"|"right"|"both"|"none" bypasses JS and forces the attributes ("both" = data-top-bottom-scroll for vertical, data-left-right-scroll for horizontal).
ScrollShadow.openQuestions: ScrollShadow.visibility does not fit the single-attr shape of attrProps; see valueMap. Semantics of top/bottom/left/right were derived from the CSS gradients (top-scroll = 0deg gradient fading the top edge; left-scroll = 270deg fading the left edge), not from a render.

Group hover: native :hover or data-hovered; focus ring: native :focus-within or data-focus-within="true" on the group. --color-field-border-invalid (invalid border) is undeclared anywhere: outline still shows, border-color fallback unverified. fullWidth needs BOTH search-field--full-width on root and search-field__group--full-width on the group; variant is the root class only (.search-field--secondary .search-field__group).

Separator.notes: Single element, no children. React resolves orientation = prop ?? SeparatorContext.orientation (Toolbar sets the OPPOSITE axis) ?? "horizontal", and always emits class separator + separator--<orientation> + separator--<variant> (variant default "default" so separator--default is always present), data-slot="separator", data-orientation=<orientation>. RAC element/attrs: horizontal renders <hr role="separator"> (role is always set because the elementType prop is unset; no aria-orientation); vertical renders <div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical"> (hr is swapped for div). Static: use hr for horizontal, div for vertical. Sizing: horizontal h-px w-full; vertical w-px, self-stretch, min-h-2 (needs a flex/grid parent with height). Inside .toolbar the rules .toolbar .separator--vertical (height 50%) and .separator--horizontal (width 50%) apply, so the orientation class must match the perpendicular axis (see Toolbar). Other components select it by attribute, so keep data-slot="separator" (and data-orientation) when used inside them: .list-box [data-slot=separator][data-orientation=horizontal], .dropdown__menu [data-slot=separator], .menu [data-slot=separator] (width:94%; margin-left:3%). separator__container, separator__container--horizontal/--vertical, separator__line, separator__content, separator__content--horizontal/--vertical exist only in CSS: React never emits them (absent from @heroui/react dist) and Separator renders no content. A labelled divider (flex container > line + content + line) is therefore a CSS-only pattern whose intended markup is unverified.

propTargets.animationType: Root (class skeleton--<type>; default read from :root CSS var --skeleton-animation, not a data attribute)

Skeleton.notes: Single div; React emits no data-slot, no role and no aria attributes, and no children. Classes: skeleton + skeleton--<animationType>. animationType default: when the prop is undefined React reads the CSS var --skeleton-animation from :root (HeroUI theme sets it to shimmer) and falls back to the tv default shimmer; "none" emits skeleton--none (inert). Static HTML must write the modifier class explicitly. No intrinsic size: the author must size/shape it (width, height, rounded-*) with extra classes or inline style. Shimmer is an ::after bar (keyframes "skeleton": translateX -100% to 200%, 2s linear infinite, defined in heroui.min.css); pulse uses animation:var(--animate-pulse) (opacity); both are disabled by prefers-reduced-motion and an ancestor [data-reduce-motion=true]. Group shimmer is pure CSS and works statically: a .skeleton--shimmer element that contains .skeleton descendants (:has(.skeleton)) drops its own ::after, draws a single ::before overlay sweeping the whole container, and suppresses the children ::after. So wrap placeholders in div.skeleton.skeleton--shimmer with child div.skeleton elements. (The source CSS carries a TODO: "Skeleton with parent are not visible".)

Slider.notes:
DOM: div.slider[data-slot=slider][role=group][data-orientation=horizontal|vertical] > [label[data-slot=label]] + [output.slider__output[data-slot=slider-output]] + div.slider__track[data-slot=slider-track][data-orientation][data-fill-start][data-fill-end] > div.slider__fill[data-slot=slider-fill] + div.slider__thumb[data-slot=slider-thumb] (one per value). data-orientation on the ROOT is REQUIRED (all track/thumb sizing is under .slider[data-orientation=...]; React defaults horizontal). Label needs data-slot='label' (grid placement); output text = value, range values joined with ' – ' (en dash, spaces around).
TRACK EDGE FLAGS (HeroUI computes; set by hand, 'true' or omit): single thumb: data-fill-start when value>min, data-fill-end when value==max; two thumbs: data-fill-start when first thumb is at min, data-fill-end when last thumb is at max. They colour the track's transparent 0.75rem side borders accent (horizontal border-inline-start/end; vertical border-bottom/top) so the fill reaches the track edges.
INLINE STYLES: FILL horizontal style='left:S%; width:W%' (S = start fraction*100, 0 for one thumb; W = (end-start)*100); vertical style='bottom:S%; height:W%'. THUMB horizontal style='left:P%', vertical 'top:(100-P)%', plus transform:translate(-50%,-50%) in both (RAC also sets position:absolute and touch-action:none; CSS supplies position, top:50% / left:50% on the cross axis, thumb sizes and the visible knob as ::after 24x16 / 16x24). P = (value-min)/(max-min)*100. RAC thumb contains a visually-hidden input[type=range] (interactivity only).
STATE: thumb data-dragging='true' (knob scales .9), data-focus-visible='true' (z-10 ring; only via attribute), data-disabled='true' on root/track/fill/thumb; root div also data-disabled='true' or aria-disabled='true' (status-disabled; :disabled never applies to a div; label stays opaque). Slider.Marks: React emits div[data-slot=slider-marks] with class slider__marks but NO CSS rule exists for it (marked TODO in source).

Spinner.notes: Root is <span class="spinner spinner--<color> spinner--<size>" data-slot="spinner"> with no role/aria on the span; the rotation (spin .75s linear infinite, off under reduced motion) is on the span itself, and colour is the span text colour (spinner--<color> sets color; the svg uses currentColor; "current" = inherit). Injected child you must write: <svg data-slot="spinner-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true" aria-label="Loading" role="presentation"> with NO width/height attributes; it fills the span, whose size is 16px sm, 24px md, 32px lg, 40px xl (svg fill-the-span layout inferred, no spinner svg CSS exists outside Toast). React also emits a third fill-less path (invisible); omit it. Gradient ids are generated per instance by React useId; in static HTML give each spinner its own unique G1/G2 ids. Keep data-slot="spinner" (span) and data-slot="spinner-icon" (svg): CSS keys on them in other components (.button svg:not([data-slot=spinner] svg) exempts spinners from button icon sizing; .toast__indicator [data-slot=spinner], [data-slot=spinner-icon] sets 16px).

Minimal static markup:

...one .switch per item...

Table.notes: Block names differ: root is div.table-root (+ table-root--primary|secondary, data-slot=table); every part is table__* (there is no .table class). Tabs.notes:
DOM: div.tabs[data-slot=tabs][data-orientation] > div.tabs__list-container (must be a DIRECT child of .tabs and parent of the list: secondary variant uses > .tabs__list-container > .tabs__list) > div.tabs__list[data-slot=tabs-list][role=tablist][aria-orientation][data-orientation] > div.tabs__tab[data-slot=tabs-tab][role=tab][id][aria-selected=true|false] (an if the tab has href); panels are siblings of the container: div.tabs__panel[data-slot=tabs-panel][role=tabpanel][id][aria-labelledby=] (tabindex=0 only when the panel has no focusable child). aria-controls= exists only on the selected tab. data-orientation="horizontal|vertical" (default horizontal) is REQUIRED on BOTH .tabs (flex-col vs flex-row) and .tabs__list (horizontal: w-full flex-row; vertical: flex-col gap-1 + separator geometry); React/RAC emits it on both. SELECTED tab: data-selected="true" on .tabs__tab (+ aria-selected="true"), and the indicator is a child INSIDE that tab only:
(RAC SelectionIndicator/SharedElement renders a div only in the selected tab; absolute inset 0, z-index -1 behind the label because .tabs__tab is position:relative z-index:1; the sliding animation is runtime inline translate/width/height and is not reproducible statically). Separator: is a CHILD of a tab (absolute at left:0 / top:0); by CSS geometry put it in every tab except the first (inferred, React does not enforce). CSS hides it (opacity 0) when its tab or the immediately preceding sibling tab is data-selected, so tabs must be adjacent siblings; display:none in the secondary variant. Non-selected panels are not rendered by RAC: add hidden (or omit) on them (no CSS hides them). Disabled tab: aria-disabled="true" + data-disabled="true". Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" on .tabs__tab (native rule :focus-visible:not(:focus) never matches); hover works natively (data-hovered forces). Panel data-entering/data-exiting/data-inert are transient runtime states.

Tag.notes: A Tag only exists inside a TagGroup, and size/variant are NOT Tag props: they come from TagGroup via context, so every static .tag must carry the cascaded modifiers itself. React always emits class="tag tag--<size> tag--<variant>" (defaults tag--md tag--default; surface -> tag--surface). DOM: div.tag[data-slot=tag][role=row] > (RAC wraps content in div[role=gridcell][style="display:contents"]) label text, optional svg icons (any svg inside .tag is forced to size-3) and the remove button. Selected: data-selected="true" (+ aria-selected="true") on .tag (accent-soft bg; no native equivalent). Disabled: data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true". Hover/focus-visible/active work natively (data-hovered, data-focus-visible, data-pressed force). Remove button is auto-injected when the group has onRemove (RAC then adds data-allows-removing="true" on the tag; no CSS): <button type="button" class="close-button close-button--default tag__remove-button" slot="remove" data-slot="tag-remove-button" aria-label="Remove tag"><svg data-slot="close-button-icon" 16x16 close x icon, aria-hidden/></button> (CloseButton contributes the close-button classes; .tag__remove-button only sets size-3 and color inherit). textValue is a11y only.

propTargets.size: Root (cascades to each Tag via context; emitted as tag--<size> class on .tag, nothing on TagGroup)
propTargets.variant: Root (cascades to each Tag via context; emitted as tag--<variant> class on .tag, nothing on TagGroup)

TagGroup.notes: DOM: div.tag-group[data-slot=tag-group] > optional label (shared Label: span.label[data-slot=label], not a tag-group part) + div.tag-group__list[data-slot=tag-group-list][role=grid, role=group when empty; data-empty="true" when no tags (no CSS)] > .tag items (see Tag) + optional description/error text. CSS adds p-1 to [slot=description], [data-slot=description], [slot=errorMessage], [data-slot=error-message] inside .tag-group; markup from the shared components: <span class="description" data-slot="description" slot="description"> and <span class="error-message" data-slot="error-message" slot="errorMessage">. size (sm|md|lg) and variant (default|surface) are TagGroup props that React puts on NO TagGroup element: they cascade via context to each Tag, where they become tag--<size>/tag--<variant>; the static author must put those classes on every .tag. Selection, removal and keyboard navigation are RAC runtime.

TextArea.notes: Static markup: <textarea class="textarea [textarea--secondary] [textarea--full-width]" data-slot="textarea">. Native element, RAC TextArea adds data attrs only. Native :hover, :focus and :disabled work (hover only in a hover:hover media query); data-hovered / data-focused / data-focus-visible = "true" force the states. Invalid: data-invalid="true" on the textarea (aria-invalid alone does not style it; RAC converts aria-invalid to data-invalid). Disabled: disabled attribute, or data-disabled="true" / aria-disabled="true". variant falls back to the TextField context when the prop is absent (see TextField: add textarea--secondary by hand). fullWidth is a prop of TextArea itself; the TextField only widens it through .textfield--full-width [data-slot=textarea]. min-height 38px and field tokens come from CSS. Label / description / error go as siblings inside the .textfield (see TextField). Note: inside an InputGroup the textarea is a different part (InputGroup.TextArea: class input-group__input, data-slot="input-group-textarea").

isDisabled.target: Root (.textfield); the inner input also needs disabled / data-disabled

propTargets.variant: Not applied to Root; cascades via TextFieldContext to Input (input--secondary), TextArea (textarea--secondary) and InputGroup (input-group--secondary)

TextField.notes: Root: <div class="textfield [textfield--full-width]" data-slot="textfield"> (RAC TextField div, no role). Children are siblings directly under the root: <label class="label" data-slot="label" for="ID">, <input class="input" data-slot="input" id="ID"> (or <textarea class="textarea" data-slot="textarea"> or an .input-group), <span class="description" data-slot="description">, <span class="field-error" data-slot="field-error" data-visible="true">. TextField CSS styles none of these: description needs class description (the only TextField rule on it is display:none when invalid), field-error needs data-visible (presence) or stays height:0/opacity:0, and .textfield--full-width [data-slot=input|textarea] {width:100%} only works if the input carries data-slot="input"/"textarea". INVALID: set data-invalid="true" on .textfield (hides every [data-slot=description] via display:none and turns [data-invalid=true] .label red) AND on the .input/.textarea itself; the red outline selector is .input[data-invalid=true] only (aria-invalid alone does nothing; RAC Input converts aria-invalid to data-invalid at runtime). aria-invalid="true" on the root is also accepted by the hide-description rule. Other root attrs RAC sets: data-disabled, data-readonly, data-required (="true"); data-required on the root puts the asterisk on a direct-child .label (or use label--required). variant is NOT a textfield class: TextFieldRoot only stores it in TextFieldContext and Input / TextArea / InputGroup read it, so the author adds input--secondary / textarea--secondary / input-group--secondary on those children.
TextField.openQuestions: generatorDraft.props lists only fullWidth, but TextFieldRoot also accepts variant (primary|secondary, default primary via inputVariants) which has no class on the root.

propTargets.fullWidth: Root (time-field--full-width); Group has its own fullWidth -> date-input-group--full-width
propTargets.variant: Group (DateInputGroup root, date-input-group--secondary); not a TimeField root prop

TimeField.notes:
Thin wrapper identical in shape to DateField: Root = RAC TimeField div.time-field[data-slot=time-field] (flex column gap-1); only prop fullWidth (time-field--full-width). Visuals come from the Group = DateInputGroup (date-input-group* classes; TimeField.Group/Input/InputContainer/Segment/Prefix/Suffix re-export the DateInputGroup parts); see DateInputGroup notes. Segments are the same span.date-input-group__segment[data-slot=date-input-group-segment] with data-type=hour|minute|second|dayPeriod (and data-type=literal for ':' and the space before AM/PM); empty ones carry data-placeholder='true' with locale-driven placeholder text.
Root children: Label (data-slot='label'), Group, Description (data-slot='description'; hidden when root has data-invalid='true' or aria-invalid='true'), FieldError. Root state attrs: data-invalid, data-disabled, data-readonly, data-required. Props not on Root: variant (and group-level fullWidth) live on the Group part.
TimeField.openQuestions: Placeholder text for empty time segments is locale-driven by RAC and was not checked.

propTargets.placement: Provider (region class; cascades to each Toast via context to give toast--<placement>)
propTargets.variant: Root (the Toast element; Indicator takes variant too, only to choose its default icon)

Toast.notes: Root part Toast IS the .toast element; Toast.Queue and Toast.toast() are non-DOM APIs. Static markup: div.toast-region.toast-region--<placement>[data-slot=toast-region][role=region][aria-label=Notifications][tabindex=-1] style="--toast-width:460px" (fixed z-50 pointer-events-none; width calc(100vw-2rem), sm:min-w-(--toast-width); React also inlines --gap:12px, --placement, --scale-factor:.05, unused by CSS) > ol > li (both display:contents, layout-neutral) > div.toast.toast--<placement>.toast--<variant>[data-slot=toast][role=alertdialog][aria-modal=false][tabindex=0][data-index=<i>][data-frontmost=true] > div.toast__indicator[data-slot=toast-indicator] + div.toast__content[data-slot=toast-content] (> span.toast__title[slot=title][data-slot=toast-title] + span.toast__description[slot=description][data-slot=toast-description]) + action + button.close-button.close-button--default.toast__close-button[data-slot=toast-close][aria-label=Close][slot=close] (its svg needs data-slot=close-button-icon: CSS sizes it). Action = HeroUI Button with extra class toast__action and data-slot=toast-action-button: after .toast__content on desktop, inside .toast__content after the description on mobile (<=768px). Placement is written twice and must match: region toast-region--bottom|bottom-start|bottom-end|top|top-start|top-end (spaces become hyphens) and each toast toast--<same>. REQUIRED STATE: data-frontmost="true" on the front toast, otherwise .toast gets pointer-events none, overflow hidden, height var(--front-height) and hides its close button; data-hidden="true" (opacity 0) for index >= 3 (default max visible). The close button is opacity 0 / pointer-events none until .toast[data-frontmost=true]:hover; to show it statically add inline opacity:1;pointer-events:auto (no data attribute does it). .toast is position:absolute left:0 right:0 (bottom:0 for bottom placements, top:0 for top) inside the zero-height region, so stacking comes from React inline styles at queue index i: scale:(1-0.05*i); translate:"0 <+-12*i>px 0" (negative for bottom, positive for top); z-index:(count-i); opacity:(hidden?0:1); pointer-events:(hidden?none:auto); --front-height:<front toast height px> (read by .toast:not([data-frontmost=true])); without them several toasts overlap exactly. Variants: toast--accent|success|warning|danger recolor the title (and indicator for success/warning/danger); React also emits toast--default (no CSS). Indicator default icon svg[data-slot=toast-default-icon] (16x16, CSS box-content size-4): default/accent = Info, success = check-circle, warning = triangle, danger = circle-exclamation; Indicator takes its own variant prop only to pick that icon. Loading: indicator holds span.spinner.spinner--current.spinner--sm[data-slot=spinner] > svg[data-slot=spinner-icon][viewBox="0 0 24 24"] (CSS size-4 on both). Enter/exit animation is driven by document.startViewTransition (React sets only an inline view-transition-name: toast-<key> per toast); the CSS rules keyed on view-transition-class names toast-top / toast-bottom are never matched because React sets no view-transition-class: not reproducible statically.
Toast.openQuestions: generatorDraft.parts has a lowercase key 'toast' (imperative toast() helper) and Queue: both non-DOM, null is correct. The Root Toast part is not listed in parts but maps to class 'toast'.

propTargets.size: Root; when absent inherited from ToggleButtonGroup via ToggleButtonGroupContext (adds toggle-button--sm|--lg)

ToggleButton.notes: Static markup: <button type="button" class="toggle-button toggle-button--default [toggle-button--sm|--lg] [toggle-button--icon-only]" data-slot="toggle-button" aria-pressed="false">. Selected: data-selected="true" is the ONLY selector (aria-pressed alone styles nothing); also set aria-pressed="true" for a11y (in a single-select ToggleButtonGroup RAC uses role="radio" aria-checked instead of aria-pressed). Disabled: disabled attribute or aria-disabled="true" (React sets data-disabled too, but CSS does not use it). Native :hover (hover:hover media) and :active work; data-hovered / data-pressed = "true" force them. Focus ring: the native selector is :focus-visible:not(:focus), which cannot match, so the ring appears only with data-focus-visible="true". Any child svg is auto-sized (size-5, sm:size-4, -mx-0.5; size-4 for --sm); there is no spinner exclusion. Inside a ToggleButtonGroup only `size` cascades (via ToggleButtonGroupContext): the author mirrors the group size by adding toggle-button--sm/--lg to each button; variant, isIconOnly and fullWidth do not cascade. TOGGLE_BUTTON_GROUP_CHILD is exported but unused by ToggleButton (unlike Button's BUTTON_GROUP_CHILD). Selected tokens (--toggle-button-bg-selected, --toggle-button-fg-selected) are declared in CSS, nothing set inline.

propTargets.size: Root (cascades to ToggleButton via ToggleButtonGroupContext; no class on the group itself)
propTargets.isDisabled: Root data-disabled + cascades to ToggleButton children by RAC state
propTargets.fullWidth: Root (toggle-button-group--full-width); CSS stretches child .toggle-button with flex:1

ToggleButtonGroup.notes:
Static markup:
containing .toggle-button children. RAC sets role=radiogroup for single selection (default selectionMode is single, verified in useToggleGroupState) and toolbar for multiple; data-orientation is emitted but CSS keys only on the --horizontal/--vertical classes (orientation class is always emitted, default horizontal); data-disabled="true" when isDisabled (no CSS on the group). CSS is structural (.toggle-button:first-child / :last-child set the outer radius; all others radius 0; pressed scale removed; focus ring inset), so keep buttons as first/last children. --detached adds gap-1, restores full radius per button and hides separators. --full-width makes children flex:1. Separator: : CSS is position:absolute (horizontal left:-1px;top:25%;width:1px;height:50%; vertical top:-1px;left:25%;width:50%;height:1px; bg currentColor at 15% opacity). The group is not positioned but .toggle-button is position:relative, so place it as the first child INSIDE each non-first .toggle-button (inferred from CSS; no usage example found in frontend-alpha). A separator as a direct group child would also break the :last-child radius rules. Cascade: only `size` reaches ToggleButtons by context (isDisabled via RAC group state disables each child, which static HTML must repeat as disabled on each button); fullWidth and isDetached are root classes only.
ToggleButtonGroup.openQuestions: Separator placement inside the next button is inferred from CSS only (no example found in frontend-alpha); confirm against HeroUI docs.

propTargets.orientation: Root (class toolbar--<o>, aria-orientation, data-orientation); cascades to ToggleButtonGroup via RAC ToggleButtonGroupContext and its opposite axis cascades to Separator via SeparatorContext

Toolbar.notes: Root: <div class="toolbar toolbar--<orientation>" data-slot="toolbar"> with RAC attributes role="toolbar" (becomes role="group" when nested inside another [role=toolbar]), aria-orientation=<orientation>, data-orientation=<orientation> (not selected by CSS; layout comes from the toolbar--vertical class) and aria-label or aria-labelledby (provide one). toolbar--horizontal is always emitted but has an empty rule. isAttached only adds toolbar--attached (rounded-3xl bg-surface p-1 shadow-overlay); no attribute. Layout is plain CSS grid (grid-flow-col, gap-2, w-fit; vertical = grid-flow-row); children are ordinary elements. Roving arrow-key navigation (Left/Right or Up/Down) is runtime-only. Context React provides to children, which the author must replicate by hand: (1) ToggleButtonGroupContext {orientation}: a ToggleButtonGroup without its own orientation prop inherits the toolbar orientation, so write toggle-button-group--horizontal|--vertical and data-orientation on the group to match the toolbar; (2) SeparatorContext {orientation: OPPOSITE of the toolbar}: a Separator without orientation is vertical in a horizontal toolbar and horizontal in a vertical one, so write class "separator separator--vertical" (div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" data-orientation="vertical" data-slot="separator") in a horizontal toolbar, or "separator separator--horizontal" (hr data-orientation="horizontal") in a vertical toolbar. CSS that depends on these: .toolbar .separator--vertical {height:50%; align-self:center}, .toolbar .separator--horizontal {width:50%; justify-self:center}, .toolbar--vertical .button-group {justify-content:flex-start}.
Toolbar.openQuestions: Whether ButtonGroup (not ToggleButtonGroup) inside Toolbar also inherits orientation was not checked; only ToggleButtonGroupContext and SeparatorContext are provided by ToolbarRoot.

Arrow.why: No BEM class; CSS targets [data-slot=overlay-arrow] (svg) inside [data-slot=tooltip-arrow] wrapper

Tooltip.notes:
Static markup: div.tooltip__trigger[role=button][tabindex=0][data-slot=tooltip-trigger] (inline-block; React wraps the trigger content in it; tabindex comes from useFocusable) and, when shown, div.tooltip[role=tooltip][id][data-placement=top|bottom|left|right] (React portals it to ); the trigger gets aria-describedby= while open. .tooltip is max-w-xs p-2 text-xs break-all with no positioning: RAC inlines style="position:absolute; z-index:100000; top/left:; max-height:" plus --trigger-anchor-point:"px px" (transform-origin only); the author positions it by hand. Default placement is top, offset 3 (7 when showArrow). data-placement must be written on .tooltip: CSS rotates [data-slot=overlay-arrow] by it (bottom 180deg, left -90deg, right 90deg, top 0) and picks the enter slide. Arrow (Tooltip.Arrow; React default showArrow=false so usually absent), a child of .tooltip:
aria-hidden=true role=presentation style="position:absolute; transform:translateX(-50%) (translateY(-50%) for left/right); :100%; left:px (top:px for left/right)">
; arrow fill/stroke CSS is keyed on data-slot=overlay-arrow (NOT popover-overlay-arrow); wrapper data-slot=tooltip-arrow has no CSS. Open/close delays come from the :root CSS vars --tooltip-delay (1.5s) and --tooltip-close-delay (.5s), read by JS only. data-entering/data-exiting="true" only drive animation (omit statically). Hover/focus-triggered opening cannot be reproduced statically; a visible tooltip is just the .tooltip element. Trigger focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true".

propTargets.type: Root (class typography--<type> and element tag); Heading.level -> h<level>, Paragraph.size -> body|body-sm|body-xs, Code -> code are preset aliases of this prop

Typography.notes: Root renders RAC Text with the tag chosen by type (React elementType map): body, body-sm, body-xs -> p; code -> code; h1..h6 -> h1..h6. Attributes: data-slot="typography", data-type=<type> (no Typography CSS selects data-type). Classes ALWAYS emitted: typography + typography--<type> (default body) + typography--align-<align> (default start) + typography--color-<color> (default default). typography--weight-* is emitted only when weight is set (no default); typography--truncate only when truncate=true (block + overflow hidden + ellipsis + nowrap, so it needs a constrained width). Sub-components are presets of the same root, not separate CSS: Typography.Heading level=1..6 (default 1) -> type h<level>, tag h<level>; Typography.Paragraph size=base|sm|xs (default base) -> type body|body-sm|body-xs, tag p; Typography.Code -> type code, tag code (typography--code = bg-default rounded-md px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-sm). They all accept the root props align, color, weight, truncate; Heading.level and Paragraph.size are aliases that resolve to type. Typography.Prose is different: <div class="typography-prose" data-slot="prose"> (no typography class, no variant props, no typography--* classes apply); it styles descendant plain HTML tags by element selector (h1-h6, p, code, a, blockquote, ul, ol, li, hr, pre, strong, em, img), so its children must be raw semantic tags, not typography classes. color only has default (--foreground) and muted (--muted).
Typography.openQuestions: Parts Code/Heading/Paragraph map to base class typography and Prose to typography-prose in the generator draft; this is correct for the base class but the real class set depends on the preset type (see notes), so no partFixes given.
